News.title: Zelensky lashes out at EU
News.content:
Volodymyr Zelensky lashed out at the European Union over its moves to weaken sanctions on Russian oligarchs.

In his address to the UN General Assembly, the Ukrainian leader warned that beyond making life “more comfortable” for Russians, “it also gives the war more time for Putin to send poor people into the kill zone. So Russia’s revenues must remain a target.”

His criticism came after France and Luxembourg successfully pushed for sanctions exemptions for Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman, Russian oligarchs, on Tuesday.

Kyiv branded the decision “shameful and unjustifiable”. The men are known to share close ties to Vladimir Putin and have net worths of $14bn and $16bn, respectively.

In his fourth address to the UN as a wartime leader, Mr Zelensky said it was paramount that the international community increased pressure on the Kremlin to stop “the madness” of the war spreading.

Under pressure from Donald Trump to halt attacks on Russian energy targets, Mr Zelensky defended his country’s aerial offensive for successfully depriving Putin of revenue for his war.

“When someone gives Russia more money through trade, they give this war more time. And that is exactly why we insist on limiting trade with the aggressor, and why we are burning Russia’s revenues ourselves,” he said.

‘End the war before winter’

Washington has recently attempted to revive the long-stalled negotiations between Ukraine and Russia. On Tuesday, Mr Zelensky implored Mr Trump to help Kyiv end the war “before winter”.

Mr Trump appeared optimistic, suggesting an agreement would happen “more quickly than people understand”.

Sergei Lavrov, the Russian foreign minister, told the UN Security Council on Wednesday that Russia was prepared to negotiate for a lasting peace but would not “pause the war”.

Mr Zelensky sought to remind world leaders that the conflict was not constrained within Ukraine’s borders at a time when the global community was distracted by a myriad of conflicts and crises.

Citing the support of Iran and North Korea for Russia, he warned that Putin’s war kept “spreading further”.

“Putin is always looking for someone who can help him kill more, kill more people for every kilometre of land, take more territory and take another country instead of simply stopping and running his own country,” Mr Zelensky said at the UN.

He noted that fighters from at least 47 countries were helping to prosecute Moscow’s war against Ukraine and urged leaders to prevent their citizens from being dragged into the conflict.

After Mr Zelensky’s address, reports emerged that Kirill Dmitriev, Putin’s envoy, was on his way to the US where he would meet Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, the Trump administration representatives.

Sources told Reuters that the meeting would take place in New ‌York on the sidelines of the UN summit.

Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, also confirmed Mr Trump had invited his Russian counterpart to attend the G20 summit of world leaders in Miami in December.

News.title: Male contraceptives could hit pharmacies in ‘three to five years’, says WHO
News.content:
Game-changing contraceptives for men could be on pharmacy shelves as soon as 2029, according to the World Health Organization.

Speaking to the Telegraph, Dr James Kiarie, head of the UN agency’s contraception and fertility care unit, said he expects male birth control to be available in just a few years, in a major expansion of contraceptive options for men.

“In three to five years, we will actually have a method available, [so] men can be more than supporters of their female partners in using contraception – men can actually be users,” he said.

On Tuesday, the WHO released its first Target Product Profiles (TPPs) for these products, setting out guidelines for the desired and minimum standards any male contraceptive product must meet.

“[The TPPs] signals that this is a priority issue for the WHO,” said Dr Kiarie.

“Currently men do not have much option in terms of their contraceptive methods. They have to either use condoms… [or] they have to use withdrawal, which has a high failure rate, or they have to use vasectomy, which is a permanent method.”

At the moment, the most advanced new product is called NES/T. It is a daily hormonal gel that is applied to the shoulders and upper arms, and suppresses sperm production without affecting testosterone levels.

Other candidates include injectable hydrogels that block sperm travel, an approach that has been described as a “reversible vasectomy”. ADAM, developed by Contraline, is in phase 1 trials while Next Life Sciences is set to trial a similar product called Plan A.

A third option is YCT-529 – the first non-hormonal, daily male birth control pill. It is currently in phase 1b and 2a clinical trials.

Dr Kiarie said it was important to have multiple options as “there’s no one size fits all” approach, but warned development could take longer than five years if clinical trials face unexpected hurdles.

News.title: England learn more in scrappy Sri Lanka win than in summer of white-ball walkovers
News.content:
You do not expect spinners to dominate at Chester-le-Street, but this hot summer has produced strange events, none more so than Jacks recording the second-best figures by an England spinner in one-day international cricket having previously only taken three wickets in 16 games at home.

Sachindu Colombage, Sri Lanka’s debutant leggie who was playing club cricket in East Anglia a year ago, laid down a marker as he impressed with three for 44 starting with the wicket of Root, his first dismissal in one-day international cricket since February.

England’s 89-run win was completed by Jacks taking three for none in four balls as Sri Lanka were bowled out for 176, their run chase a timid effort when they had a sniff of victory after restricting England to 265 and preventing them from hitting a six for the first time in an innings since 2019.

Vice-captain Jacks has evolved under Harry Brook’s leadership from an opening batsman to middle-order finisher who can chip in with the ball. “He is just a good leader with bat ball and in the field. He is buying into everything we want to do,” Brook said. “We are always talking about adapting to conditions and he has done it really well since coming back in. He could have moaned and groaned about batting in the middle order and playing as an all-rounder but has accepted that will be his place for a long time.”

Brook thought England made “just about par” on a very dry pitch and was reluctant to shower too much praise on batting consultant Kevin Pietersen, whose spin class the day before concentrated on making runs on a slow surface. “It will take time, more than one day. He’s not a miracle worker but it helps the more opportunity we get,” Brook said.

England were stretched and Pietersen will be happy. He told them to think about their approach, that in this type of game “rotation of strike is incredibly important”. He was right, they ran well, apart from Rehan Ahmed, and did not hit a six in an innings for the first time in seven years.

When England batsmen tried to force the pace they perished. Ben Duckett, Root and Brook all had opportunities to build an innings without seeing it through and it required Jacks to tip the total to more than 250. He batted within himself at first, but hit four fours in a row in the 47th over in a late burst that took England to a winning score.

News.title: Africa faces new threat as chronic disease rate leaps
News.content:
Chronic ailments like heart disease, cancers and diabetes now account for almost half of deaths in Africa and will soon overtake the continent’s infectious disease toll, new research has found.

Between 1990 and 2023 the proportion of deaths caused by non-communicable diseases (NCDs) almost doubled, from 25 per cent to 45 per cent, with heart disease and strokes now the leading killers.

The shift is not unexpected: public health experts have long warned that although African countries are making huge strides cutting infectious disease deaths through vaccinations, better sanitation and improved healthcare, lifestyle changes pose a new threat.

But the continent is not necessarily ready to tackle this “epidemiological transition”, researchers warned, in a study published in the Lancet Global Health journal on Tuesday.

“Although the epidemiological transition is well recognised, the speed and scale of NCD growth in Africa is particularly concerning,” they wrote.

“Health systems face increasing demands for chronic disease management, yet low-resource settings remain poorly equipped, underfunded, and unable to provide adequate preventive or treatment services.”

News.title: Zika mosquitoes still breeding in London
News.content:
Dr Medlock said there is still “no conclusive” evidence about how the insects arrived, but it’s possible that someone brought them back from holiday in their luggage, or that mosquito eggs were hidden on a tropical plant.

The mosquitoes are very temperature sensitive – they typically survive and multiply between 25C and 30C – and the UK has historically been too cold. But the species are gradually making their way north through Europe, after successive summers of record heat.

As temperatures drop in the coming weeks, the UKHSA hopes London’s invasive mosquitoes will die off naturally – though an unprecedented El Niño has made the predicament more challenging.

“This is a tropical mosquito, so the model has convinced me this won’t survive the winter,” Dr Medlock said. “Although we’ve got El Niño, [so] it’s very mild – it’s certainly warm enough still in East London [for the insects to survive].”

Diseases such as dengue and Zika virus do not typically circulate in Britain, but an infected traveller returning from a country where the diseases are present could carry the virus back with them.

If an invasive mosquito then bit an infected person, it could potentially catch and spread on the disease to others.

Several countries in Europe, including France, Italy and Spain, have started to see local transmission of mosquito-borne viruses, including dengue fever and West Nile virus, in recent years as the climate becomes more suitable for mosquitoes to survive and multiply.

Just last week, a third person died in Frankfurt, Germany, from malaria despite having no travel history, after mosquitoes infected with the disease were imported into the country on an aeroplane and subsequently infected eight people over the summer.

“We [already] see imported cases of malaria, dengue and chikungunya each year, with significant associated mortality and morbidity,” Dr Phillip Veal, a consultant in public health at the UKHSA, said.

“But if we [in Britain] follow the pattern of Europe, and all models suggest we will, Aedes albopictus and other Aedes species may become established. We’ve got a window of opportunity to do something, to prepare, to be ready, to fulfil our mission of protecting the public,” Dr Veal said.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Tax rises ‘virtually inevitable’ after £8bn borrowing blow
News.content:
Tax rises are “virtually inevitable” after official figures showed the Treasury has borrowed £8bn more than expected so far this year.

Economists said the Chancellor faced an “uncomfortable” Budget after the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said spending outstripped tax receipts by £18.3bn in August, £3.5bn more than expected.

It means John Healey, the Chancellor, has borrowed £77.3bn so far this financial year, which is £8.1bn more than forecast.

Reacting to the figures, Emma Reynolds, the Chief Secretary to the Treasury, warned of “tough decisions” in Mr Healey’s Budget.

Thomas Pugh, chief economist at RSM UK, said: “The jump in borrowing in August compared to last year sets the stage for what is likely to be a much trickier Budget than Andy Burnham or Healey anticipated when they came to power.

“Another round of tax rises in October now looks inevitable.”

Philip Shaw, an economist at Investec, added: “We suspect that some tax increases are virtually inevitable.”

Ruth Gregory, deputy chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said the Chancellor would need to raise up to £14bn to restore the £24bn of fiscal headroom left by his predecessor Rachel Reeves to balance the books.

The Government’s debt interest bill soared to £8.8bn last month, according to the ONS, the biggest August figure since records began in 1997.

So far this year, the Treasury has spent £50bn on debt interest – £2bn more than forecast in March.

Nick Ridpath, an economist at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, said: “Debt interest spending is a worryingly large share of overall government spending.

“Both higher borrowing costs and higher inflation make life harder for a Chancellor who is looking to bring down borrowing and to spend more on government priorities.”

Higher prices caused by the Iran war mean the Chancellor must pay more interest on the country’s huge stock of inflation-linked debt.

Inflation is also pushing up the welfare bill. The Government spent almost £30bn in August on benefits, 7pc more than a year ago.

Despite this, the Treasury continued to see substantial tax receipts. Income tax, capital gains, and National Insurance receipts stood at £231bn in the financial year to August.

That is £16.6bn higher than the same period a year ago.

Inheritance tax receipts also grew. They have risen to £3.8bn so far this financial year, a £100m increase compared with a year ago.

Ms Reynolds, the Treasury minister, said: “At a time when debt interest costs billions of pounds that could otherwise be spent on improving lives, we must always know where the money is coming from to pay for public services.

“That is why we are committed to meeting our fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty.”

The figures also showed total debt rose to £2.985tn in August, taking the level just shy of £3tn.

Andrew Griffith, the shadow chancellor, said: “Labour has lost control of the public finances.

“It takes a rare fiscal incontinence to have both the highest tax take in history and see borrowing still shoot up.”

News.title: France releases infertile Asian tiger mosquitoes to fight dengue threat
News.content:
French cities are fighting the growing threat of diseases like dengue, chikungunya and Zika in mainland Europe by releasing millions of sterile male Asian tiger mosquitoes.

Terratis, a new company in the southern city of Montpellier, is breeding infertile males on an industrial scale as a long-term solution to the rapid spread of the disease-carrying insects.

The sterile males are bred at a factory in the southern city of Montpellier and then released in urban hot zones where the mosquitoes are most prevalent. After they have mated, females reproduce only empty eggs for the remainder of their lives.

“By using this technique, the mosquitoes will have no descendants and then, in theory, we can reduce the population with each generation,” said Clelia Oliva, the founder of Terratis.

“We are confident of being able to achieve a reduction of between 70 and 90 per cent in the towns in which we are releasing the sterile mosquitoes.”

The company, which started only two years ago, has experienced a dramatic surge in demand in the last few years as France tries to deal with the invasive species.

Sports.title: George Gillett dead aged 87: Former Liverpool owner and businessman passes away after battle with Alzheimer’s
Sports.content:
REST IN PEACE George Gillett dead aged 87: Former Liverpool owner and businessman passes away after battle with Alzheimer’s







Next

FORMER Liverpool owner George Gillett has died at the age of 87.

The American businessman has passed away after a battle with Alzheimer’s Disease.



Gillett was the co-owner of the Reds following the takeover of the club with Tom Hicks in 2007.

The pair owned the Premier League giants before cashing in to John Henry’s New England Sports Ventures in October 2010.



Football was not the only interest of Gillett’s, who also owned the ice hockey team Montreal Canadiens and held stakes in the NFL franchise the Miami Dolphins.

Gillett also had a stake in the iconic basketball team the Harlem Globetrotters.

His death was confirmed by a statement from Canadiens owner Geoff Molson.

He said: “On behalf of the entire Canadiens organisation, I would like to extend my deepest condolences to George’s family.



“George immersed himself in the Montreal community and was appreciated by everyone in the organisation.

“We sincerely appreciate his contributions to the Montreal Canadiens during his time as owner.”

The Gillett and Hicks reign at Anfield was not a successful one after their takeover.



Fans protested against their ownership and they clashed with manager Rafael Benitez.

They eventually agreed to sell the club for roughly £300m to the group that would become the Fenway Sports Group.

During their reign the club failed to win any silverware.

The club did achieve a second-place finish in the 2008/09 season, in which Steven Gerrard top-scored with 24 goals in all competitions.

Despite this, tributes have still flooded in for the businessman on social media.



One posted: “Rest in peace.”

A second commented: “Thoughts with his family and loved ones.”

A third wrote: “Rest in peace to a great man. Peace and love to his family.”

A fourth said: “George Gillett Jr former owner of the Montreal Canadians passed away today. Some say the saviour of the franchise RIP.”

Another added: “Condolences to his family.”



National Hockey League (NHL) commissioner Gary Bettman said: “George Gillett’s passion for the Montreal Canadiens and commitment to the city of Montreal were demonstrated throughout his tenure as owner of the storied franchise from 2001 to 2009.

“He guided the Canadiens through a significant chapter in their history that included preparations for their Centennial Celebration, which honoured the franchise’s rich legacy and seminal place in our game.

“George was a friend whose company I always enjoyed, whose counsel was wise, and whose energy was contagious.

“His contributions to the hockey world left an enduring mark, and his legacy will continue to be felt throughout the game for years to come.

“The National Hockey League sends its heartfelt condolences to his family and many friends.”

Sports.title: ‘I’ll tell you how big he is’ – Craig Bellamy reveals Cristiano Ronaldo story that left Wales boss gobsmacked
Sports.content:
Next

CRISTIANO RONALDO is so big that he gets presidential treatment in Portugal.

The football legend — still playing at 41 — looks set to start the farewell leg of his incredible career against Wales in the Nations League tonight.



Ronaldo confirmed the World Cup in the summer would be his last and he was in tears after Portugal’s last-16 exit to eventual winners Spain.

But he has been named in Jorge Jesus’ first squad and there have been no signs yet he will follow great rival Lionel Messi into international football retirement.



Wales boss Craig Bellamy, who last shared a pitch with the ex-Manchester United and Real Madrid forward playing for West Ham at Old Trafford back in October 2008, hailed Ronaldo’s greatness.

Bellamy, 47, who was Burnley assistant between 2022-24, said: “We’re talking about not just one of the greatest players of our generation, we’re talking all generations with what he has been able to do.



“His professionalism, cleverness and he’s still got that habit of goalscoring and you never lose that. He’s beyond a superstar.

“But I’ll tell you how big he is. I was with Burnley on pre-season in Lisbon. We got to the airport and the police were everywhere — it was on lockdown.

“We’re Burnley and we had a little bit of VIP.

Sports.title: Football fans could be allowed to drink in stands for first time in 40 years as Labour launches bid to rip-up booze ban
Sports.content:
Next

FOOTBALL fans are set to be allowed to drink in the stands for the first time in 41 years.

Labour wants to axe the 1985 act which bans boozing in view of the pitch but does not apply to supporters in any other sports.



PM Andy Burnham said tonight there was a “case to remove that discrimination perhaps on a trial basis”. He risks a row with cops but fan groups rejoiced.

For 41 years the act has applied in the top five men’s divisions in England and Wales, plus Scotland.



Everton-supporting PM Andy said supporters had been “singled out” as fans of other sports, such as cricket and rugby, can drink while watching the action.

In New York tonight, he said football was “very different” when the 1985 Sporting Events (Control of Alcohol) Act was introduced by the Conservatives to tackle hooliganism.

The PM added: “There is a case to remove that discrimination. There are different ways it could be done, perhaps on a trial basis.

“But I’m not going to back away from what’s been a long-held view of mine. I don’t see how it can be fair that some supporters of one sport can be treated differently.”



Tom Greatrex, of The Football Supporters’ Association agreed that the act is “outdated”.

He said: “We have always argued it’s unfair to criminalise fans for having a pint while watching the match — especially since you can sit in the same seat drinking alcohol while watching an Oasis gig or rugby league.”

A recent pilot had worked in the women’s game, he added.



Mr Burnham raised the issue before becoming PM after being seen drinking a pint watching rugby league at Everton’s new Hill Dickinson Stadium.

The 2021 Fan-Led Review of Football Governance first recommended trials of terrace boozing to aid lower league clubs — projecting League 2 sides could get £4.4 million extra a season in sales.

But the UK Football Policing Unit said: “It would be incredibly rash to make fundamental changes without a full examination of the evidence and consultation with police practitioners who have expertise in this.”

MR Burnham was given tickets worth £677 for the directors’ lounge at Everton in August, the MPs’ register of interests reveals

THE CASE FOR... By Alex James, Blur star, Bournemouth fan FOOTBALL matches are about the only times crowds all sing together instinctively and without any accompanying music. To be winning and singing, with all your mates is one of the greatest feelings there is. I always feel more like singing after a couple of beers so I’m all for a couple à la terrace. A piping hot cider would hit the spot in the dark depths of February. But as the world’s greatest guzzlers, can we be trusted? Before the Premier League, our football was marred by alcohol- fuelled hooliganism and violence. We never want to go back there. But I do think the FA should treat us like adults. You can drink beer while you watch your favourite band so why not your team? Drinking beer and watching football at the same time would reunite two great institutions. In a challenging world, it’s surely every Brit’s basic birthright.

Sports.title: PSG and World Cup star Achraf Hakimi will stand trial for rape after losing latest attempt to have case thrown out
Sports.content:
Next

ACHRAF HAKIMI will stand trial for rape after losing his bid to have the case thrown out.

It was announced in June that the PSG and Morocco star would go on trial for an alleged assault on a woman in February 2023.



Hakimi, who vehemently denies the allegation, tried to get the case thrown out by lodging a motion to dismiss it with a French appeals court.

But on Wednesday, the Cour de cassation rejected his bid to have the case struck off, meaning The Atlas Lions’ talismanic skipper will have to go in the dock to address the allegation.



After the ruling, the woman’s lawyer, Rachel-Flore Pardo, said: “After three and a half years of legal battle, after being slandered and dragged through the mud by Achraf Hakimi‘s defence, my client is determined to obtain justice and will fight to the end.

“She sincerely hopes that this trial will help other women and further crack the fortress of denial and impunity surrounding sexual violence, even in the world of men’s football.”



Hakimi’s lawyer, Fanny Colin, told Le Monde when approached for comment: “The facts reproached to Achraf Hakimi, which he has firmly contested from the first day, have not been examined by the Cour de cassation.

“They will be during the trial, in the course of which all the elements in defence of Mr Achraf Hakimi will be publicly and contradictorily presented.

“Mr Hakimi, who has nothing to hide, has for his part fully cooperated with the police and judicial authorities and will continue to do so on the occasion of the forthcoming trial.”

Hakimi, who is in contention to win the Ballon d’Or, has maintained his innocence since the allegation was made against him.



In an interview with Canal+ last September, he said of the accusation last September: “For me, it’s the hardest thing that’s ever happened to me.

“And the truth is, it’s the hardest blow I’ve ever suffered. I think it was pretty hard for me, and it still is, because when they keep telling lie after lie, it hurts.

“It hurts for my family, for my children, who are young and don’t know what the internet or reading is.

“I know that at some point in their lives they’ll read things, and for me, seeing that something about their father has been written and on top of that, it’s a lie, is not very pleasant, and I honestly wouldn’t wish that on them.



“I think my lawyer told me so. We knew this could happen. We’re calm. I know what I’ve been accused of. It’s a lie. I know who I am. I know I haven’t done anything.

“And I never would. I asked to speak to the police, to them, to explain my version.

“Always when they’ve needed me for anything… What’s more, they have my DNA.

“Whatever they needed, I was available, unlike the person accusing me, who didn’t make things easy.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Thanks to the police’s work, we’ve been able to find quite a few good things.



“The truth is, I’m calm. I know I’m in good hands with my lawyer. Justice is doing its work, and I hope the truth comes out soon.”

Sports.title: Harry Kane insists he ‘trusts’ the five England stars who pulled out of Nations League clash with Spain

HARRY KANE “trusts” the five stars who pulled out of England’s clash with world champs Spain on Saturday.

Declan Rice, Cole Palmer, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento are all unavailable for four Nations League games due to fitness concerns.



England’s skipper said: “I know the guys, I’ve spoken to the coach.

“Everyone has their own situation. I know how tough the summer was and I know, especially in the Premier League, how gruelling that schedule is.



“I’m in a different situation now where I have the winter break [in Germany] and I have moments to recharge. Some of the players don’t get that.

“Everyone has to look after themselves and put themselves first, and I trust all the boys.”

Kane, 33, previously criticised nine withdrawals from a squad in 2024, saying: “England comes before anything.”

But the Bayern Munich star, who received a personal message from Rice to explain his decision, added: “Dec voice-noted me.

“I know Dec goes far and beyond for the club and country, so I know how much he gives and I know he’s been struggling for a while with his issues.

“Someone like Dec has to get himself sorted and get himself fresh, and he has big games for club, big games for the country coming up.

“The togetherness that we have, I don’t think will change with the people not being here right now.

“All it does is give other people an opportunity to impress the manager and impress the team.”

A bigger surprise than Rice’s withdrawal was the decision of Chelsea midfielder Palmer not to report after missing out on the World Cup.



Asked if he has been in contact, Kane said: “I’ve not spoken to Cole, no. Dec just reached out to me just personally.

Wieke Kaptein scored a stunning goal but Chelsea were given a stern test by Austria Wien as they began their Women's Champions League campaign with a hard-fought 1-0 win at Plough Lane.

Sports.title: Does Littler need to change approach to hostile crowds?
Sports.content:
Following Luke Littler's latest run-in with a hostile crowd over the weekend, the Sky Sports Love The Darts Podcast has debated whether it is time for the world champion to change his approach.

Littler's bid for a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 was ended on Sunday after a crushing 10-4 defeat to Jonny Clayton in the last eight at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam, but the action was overshadowed by the Brit's unhappiness at being repeatedly whistled at by the Dutch crowd.

After facing significant hostility during his win over home favourite Danny Noppert on Friday, Littler threatened to boycott future tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled at during his victory over Nathan Aspinall on Saturday, prompting referee Charlie Corstorphine to intervene.

Littler has taken a stance against volatile crowds before, refusing to travel to European Tour events in Germany as a result of his treatment from fans there.

On the latest episode of the Love The Darts Podcast, World Series of Darts Finals champion Ross Smith explained his own approach to hostile crowds, which he admits is inspired by three-time world champion Michael van Gerwen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jonny Clayton ended Luke Littler's clean sweep at the World Series of Darts Finals. Credit: @OfficialPDC.

"It's a real difficult situation," Smith said. "I can't speak for Luke because I'm not him and I wasn't in his position, I wasn't on stage at the time. I didn't really experience the whistling too much. I try not to rise to it because I know you're just going to get more stick.

"My manager once said to me, if you look at Michael van Gerwen, he never reacts, not once will he ever react to the crowd. He'll always thank them and he never really gets too much stick and he's very professional about how he does things. So, I admire him for that and I try and learn off of other people.

"I had a bit with Kevin Doets, obviously the crowd, rightly so, they're cheering their local guy on. Same with Gian [van Veen], they're doing exactly the same, but I think if you're aggressive towards the crowd and you're letting them know that it's affecting you and you're making them unhappy, it's not a good thing.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love The Darts, Ross Smith feels he is ready to play in the Premier League.

"I tried to, with Gian, I had more banter with them, you know what I mean? Just like thumbs up to them, but smiling, not in an aggressive way and they sort of laugh with you, it's not a problem.

"I think it's how you can react on stage, if you're aggressive towards them, it's going to create problems for you. But like I said, I can't really comment on Luke because I wasn't playing in the games with Luke and I don't know what he actually went through, but they can be brutal at times."

Nicholson: Maybe Littler can learn from others

Former world championship quarter-finalist Paul Nicholson praised Smith's approach, and suggested that Littler could benefit from learning from some of his rivals.

Nicholson, who himself was known for often having fractious interactions with crowds, also pointed to the way 2021 world champion Gerwyn Price has adapted his behaviour on stage.

Following on from Smith's comments, Nicholson said: "That's a really, really good way of looking at it, what Ross has just said, because from my standpoint, I tried to be aggressive because I wanted to be different and it was something that I had my entire career for, more than 10 years.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love The Darts, Paul Nicholson has backed Luke Littler's reduced schedule for the rest of the season.

"Gerwyn Price has taken years to figure it out. Now he gives the smile with the aggression, and the crowd are with him more than they ever have been.

"So, it just goes to show that Ross is looking at this right, in order to make sure that his career is in the right place moving forward.

"So, we learn from mistakes, but we actually learn from what other people are going through as well. We don't want to see Littler not going to events, but maybe he can learn from what other people are doing as well."

What could the rest of Littler's year look like? Why whistling is worse than booing for players

Nicholson also explained why Littler and other players may become particularly frustrated at being whistled.

He added: "We have seen Littler have some banter with the crowd, which we're all for by the way, because we want people to have that connection. One of the greatest things about this sport is that there is a connection between the fans and the stars.

"But what we have at the minute is a trend of people using whistling as a way to make themselves feel heard. Dart players don't like it because it's piercing. It gets in your ear and it happens in a very short, sharp way, and it comes from nowhere.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mark Webster and Michael Bridge discuss Luke Littler's concerns over crowd whistling at the World Series of Darts in Amsterdam, the potential impact on his future and whether more can be done to tackle the issue.

"You don't know if it's going to come when you're throwing a match dart, a leg dart, or even going for a treble. If it comes out of nowhere, it can put you off and your shoulder jolts, and you don't want that.

"A boo is a lesser frequency and it's more mundane, you can handle them a lot better. But these short, sharp whistles, which is what they are, they're horrible.

"And the worst thing is, if it happens once, you are thinking about whether it's going to happen again, and you can't fully focus."

Sports.title: Sedlacek wins first PDC Pro Tour title at Players Championship 30
Sports.content:
Karel Sedlacek secured his first PDC Pro Tour title at Players Championship 30, beating Scott Williams 8-7 despite a late scare as he closed in on victory.

It was a thrilling encounter, with Sedlacek outlasting Williams' barrage of high scores, which included nine maximums, but both players struggled to close out the victory, with the Czech missing five match darts.

Sedlacek would ultimately claim victory, becoming the first Czech player to win a PDC tour title. But after mounting an epic comeback, winning two of the final three legs, Williams cut a furious figure after the match, shaking hands with his opponent and the officials before throwing his darts onto the ground.

Sedlacek would go 7-5 up before nerves set in, with the 47-year-old needing to check out on 24 to win, before missing a trio of match darts, allowing Williams to pull back a leg.

The momentum turned to Williams, who hit two 140s in the resulting leg, before he pulled the contest back to 7-7.

Image: Scott Williams almost staged an incredible comeback, pulling level at the end after going 7-5 down

In the deciding leg, it looked as though the Englishman was set to produce a remarkable comeback victory, hitting a maximum to leave himself 112 to win the match, but he too stumbled, hitting five on his second dart when a single 20 would have double 16.

Williams shook his head and exclaimed, 'you're kidding me', before hitting 15 with his final dart.

It left Sedlacek the chance to check out from 32, first missing double 16 inside, subsequently missing double eight, before he finally sealed the match.

Sedlacek, who hit a match-high checkout of 164 in the ninth leg, finished the final with a checkout success of 34.8 per cent, while Williams ended with 36.8 per cent.

Sedlacek, who lauded his opponent Williams as a "good player" after the match, booked his spot in the final by beating some top opponents, including Damon Heta in the round of 32, Nathan Aspinall in the last 16 and Chris Dobey in the quarter-final, before besting Niels Zonneveld 7-2 in the semi-finals.

"It means everything," he said. "I've played for more than 30 years and now I've done it. I'm at the top of my career now and I'm really happy.

Sports.title: Giants QB Dart ruled out for 2026 season with knee injury
Sports.content:
New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart will miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season due to a knee injury.

Dart was injured on the first drive on Monday night against the Los Angeles Rams when his left leg bent awkwardly as he was hit by two defenders.

After initially saying it was in the neighborhood of a medial collateral ligament injury, coach John Harbaugh said on Tuesday the evaluation process for Dart was still ongoing.

Sports.title: Scheffler and Burns partner for Thursday fourballs at Presidents Cup
Sports.content:
Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns will take on Min Woo Lee and Sungjae Im in the first match of Thursday's fourballs at the Presidents Cup.

Brandt Snedeker's Team USA are looking to extend their winning streak to 11 consecutive victories over the International team at Medinah Country Club.

Cameron Young and Xander Schauffele head out in match two and will take on Hideki Matsuyama and Ryo Hisatsune.

Image: USA team Captain Brandt Snedeker said he was excited about his pairings

Cameron Young and Xander Schauffele will head out in match two and will take on Hideki Matsuyama and Ryo Hisatsune.

Snedeker has chosen to pair experienced Presidents Cup and Ryder Cup player Justin Thomas alongside 21-year-old rookie Jackson Koivun for match three.

They'll take on Canadian Corey Conners and Nico Echavarria of Colombia.

A blockbuster group will go out in the fourth match of the day, with two-time major champions Wyndham Clark and Collin Morikawa taking on the reigning Open champion Ryan Fox and 2013 Masters winner Adam Scott.

Chris Gotterup will pair with Patrick Cantlay in the final game of the fourballs session against Tom Kim and Si Woo Kim.

Image: International Team captain Geoff Ogilvy said he was 'pretty optimistic' about his team's chances

Match one will get under way at 5.35pm (UK and Ireland time) with the International team set to take the honours off the tee.

Thursday fourballs and tee times (all UK and Ireland time)

Match 1 (1735): Scottie Scheffler/Sam Burns vs Min Woo Lee/Sungjae Im

Match 2 (1753): Cameron Young/Xander Schauffele vs Hideki Matsuyama/Ryo Hisatsune

Match 3 (1811): Justin Thomas/Jackson Koivun vs Corey Conners/Nico Echavarria

Match 4 (1829): Wyndham Clark/Collin Morikawa vs Ryan Fox/Adam Scott

Match 5 (1847): Chris Gotterup/Patrick Cantlay vs Tom Kim/Si Woo Kim

Scheffler, Burns out to end unwanted streak

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Scheffler and Burns will be hoping to end their underwhelming run of form in team events

Scheffler and Burns have struggled together in past team events, despite being good friends, with the duo having fallen to an underwhelming record of 0-3-1 at the Presidents Cup and Ryder Cup.

"Do I think we have unfinished business? I don't know if I would call it that," Burns said.

"It's been frustrating the times we have played together, and we feel like we've played really well and ultimately not won," Burns said. "It's been more frustrating than anything.

"Yeah, this week we're going to go out and compete as hard as we can and try to get as many points for the US team as possible."

Snedeker also delved into his decision to pair up Koivun and Thomas, explaining the decision was an easy one given how well the two pair together.

"Jackson being a young kid, I feel like he's really kind of found his way on our team really quickly," Snedeker said on Wednesday. "I feel like he's handled the adjustment really well. Justin is just a natural pairing for him.

"He's somebody he's comfortable with. He'll do a great job putting his arm around him and show him how USA golf is meant to be played.

"I think we're really excited about all these match-ups and put this line-up out."

Fox taking inspiration from Europe's Ryder Cup stars

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the final day of the Presidents Cup at Royal Montreal Golf Club in Quebec, Canada

Open champion Fox is hoping the International Team can channel the energy of Team Europe at the 2025 Ryder Cup and are motivated to win for Scott.

"For us, we've always been the underdogs in this," Fox said.

"But I feel like on paper the European Ryder Cup team is always the underdogs a little bit, and that hasn't seemed to affect their results at all over the last few years.

"We're trying to channel a little bit of that and come together.

"We do have a chance to do something incredible when we've got a couple of guys on the team who have played a lot of these that we really want to get a win for. That's our motivation. I mean, Adam [Scott] especially over there.

"We're trying to flip the pressure on the US. I feel like they're expected to win, and if we can get on top early and create some pressure, there will be more pressure come on them from other places and hopefully we can take advantage of that."
