Sports.title: Northampton chief lifts lid on Pollock contract negotiations with Hearn
Sports.content:
Northampton Saints director of rugby Phil Dowson believes more players could follow Henry Pollock and work with promoters like Eddie Hearn to grow their profile.

On Tuesday, Pollock put pen to paper on a multi-year extension with his boyhood club, with the England international agreeing a deal worth £400,000 per year.

At just 21, Pollock already has 13 England caps and made five appearances for the British & Irish Lions during last year's tour of Australia.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' James Cole explains the story of Pollock signing a new contract at Northampton Saints

Pollock's profile continues to grow, with the flanker becoming the first rugby union player to join Eddie Hearn's Matchroom Talent Agency at the start of the year. Dowson revealed that the boxing promoter "drove as hard a bargain as he possibly could" during negotiations.

Reflecting on Pollock's decision to join Hearn's agency, Dowson said: "I think we'll see more of it.

"I think headlines and social media engagement, and all that, is positive for the game. Fundamentally, I talked to the coaches about this. We want more people watching the game, more people talking about the game and, ideally, most importantly, more people playing the game at loads of different age groups.

Image: Phil Dowson lauded Eddie Hearn for his role in Pollock's contract negotiations

"If Henry Pollock and Matchroom are getting some traction with the public, I think we should encourage that, but also take into account that we've got to continue to deliver that in the right way, and I think we have them."

Hearn told The Telegraph that he believes the 21-year-old is worth more than seven figures, predicting Pollock's value will "skyrocket" over the coming years while also arguing that the value of rugby will rise.

Dowson also lifted the lid on the boxing promoter's role in the negotiations, lauding him for helping him grow Pollock's profile, adding that part of the negotiations were handled by a "traditional rugby agent".

"Eddie's been excellent. He's raised the profile of the game," Dowson said.

"He's raised the profile of Henry and he's done what an agent's supposed to do. He's driven as hard a bargain as he possibly could.

"I've got a lot of respect for Eddie and how he goes about his work and some of the stuff he said in the media was really pertinent.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hearn believes that Pollock is the future of rugby and says by paying him what he deserves, he can grow the sport to another level

"I think there's elements of the contract which weren't done by Eddie, which were done by his traditional rugby agent.

"There are things from a marketing point of view and the extracurricular stuff that Eddie really looks after Pollock with, which we'll see more of.

"He wasn't necessarily doing every single negotiation from a rugby point of view."

Pollock has explained in the past that he had an open mind to the next steps of his career, but on Tuesday said he was "massively happy to re-sign with Saints".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hearn had previously said that Pollock was worth at least £1m

Some fans had questioned why the negotiations had taken so long to complete, with the flanker's loyalty coming under scrutiny, but Dowson said the process was made easier by Pollock's desire to stay.

"It's still his job, it's still his career. He needs to make sure he's getting the right deal for his aspirations and all those other elements that come with it," Dowson said. "I don't just mean from a financial point of view; I mean from a full, holistic perspective."

"Would there be loyalty in sport if he wasn't offered a contract? Would that be us not being loyal? I think we've got to be careful around that.

"He's playing really well. He's got lots of people talking about rugby. That's great. We wanted to keep him and he wanted to stay. That's a great position for us to start negotiations from, and that's the great thing about sport.

"People can have an opinion around it, but I don't think it was overly dragged out, to be honest, and I don't think it was ever done... there was no animosity in any way from my perspective."

Sports.title: Andy Burnham signals he may lift ban on alcohol in football stands
Sports.content:
Andy Burnham has signalled he may lift the ban on drinking alcohol in the stands at football matches, suggesting it is “unfair” for fans to be singled out when it is permitted for other sports.

The prime minister, a committed Everton fan who still attends matches, said there was a case for trialling an end to the ban to bring football in line with rugby and cricket.

The move was welcomed by the Football Supporters’ Association and the English Football League, but police warned it would be “incredibly rash” to make changes without considering their impact on safety.

Burnham has long opposed the ban, saying it is discriminatory and out of date, harking back to an era when football violence was fuelled by drinking within view of the pitch.

Asked by reporters on the plane to New York about lifting a ban, Burnham said: “I don’t think it’s fair for football fans to be singled out in that way and I made that point. I think that legislation dates to an era where football was very different. And I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination.

“There are different ways it could be done, perhaps on a trial basis. But I’m not going to back away from what’s been a long-held view of mine. I don’t see how it can be fair that some supporters of one sport can be treated differently.”

The Sporting Events (Control of Alcohol etc) Act 1985 prohibits drinking in sight of the pitch in England and Wales.

The fan-led review of football governance in 2021 called for the ban to be re-examined and suggested piloting the sale of alcohol within sight of the pitch in lower-tier English football.

A spokesperson for the UK Football Policing Unit, which coordinates football policing policy in England and Wales, said: “The UKFPU would welcome a meeting with the prime minister to discuss his views and explain the challenges these proposed changes would bring to policing and the safety of staff and fans at football games.

“Other sports simply don’t see the violence and criminal behaviour from their supporters that football does, albeit a minority, with alcohol often playing a significant part in violent and disorderly behaviour. It would be irresponsible to fuel this by allowing greater alcohol consumption during games.

“Following a number of football-related tragedies, changes in legislation were implemented after the Taylor report [of 1990 into the causes of the 1989 Hillsborough disaster] for good reason and we are currently in the longest ever period without a significant football-related disaster. It would be incredibly rash to make fundamental changes without a full examination of the evidence and meaningful consultation with police practitioners who have the expertise in this area.”

A spokesperson for the English Football League said it would be “receptive” to a review of legislation that “was introduced more than 40 years ago and has not kept pace with significant developments in stadium management, safety and stewarding”.

Tom Greatrex, the chair of the Football Supporters’ Association, said: “The FSA has always argued that it’s unfair to criminalise football fans for having a pint while watching the match – especially since you can sit in the same seat drinking alcohol whilst watching an Oasis gig or rugby league. We welcome the prime minister’s comments and totally agree that the legislation is outdated and deserves to be reviewed. We look forward to being part of that consultation.”

Supporters at Women’s Super League and WSL2 matches have been permitted to drink alcohol in view of the pitch since the start of this season, after a successful 18-month trial period led to a change to the WSL’s regulations this summer, allowing clubs – but not obliging them – to give fans that option.

Since that rule change, 25 of the 26 clubs across the two divisions of English women’s football have decided to take up the option at all of their home games. The only exception is Brighton & Hove Albion’s home matches at Crawley’s Broadfield Stadium, but Brighton have permitted fans to drink in view of the pitch when the team play their home matches at the Amex Stadium, such as last Sunday when they hosted Aston Villa. Women’s matches have typically seen fewer incidents of crowd trouble.

Sports.title: Harry Kane admits England’s World Cup 2026 exit ‘hurt more than any other’
Sports.content:
Harry Kane has described England’s World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina as his most painful tournament exit because of how the team lost sight of who they were.

The captain is determined to move on as quickly as possible and is chasing a statement performance against Spain at Wembley on Saturday night in the Nations League. But he admits he is yet to get over the Argentina game and knows it is something he and his England teammates must work to process.

“It felt like it wasn’t us as a team,” Kane said, as he reflected on how England lost their way in the 2-1 defeat, barely touching the ball after they went ahead in the 55th minute. “It wasn’t the team that we wanted to be and said we’d be. When you maybe go against your beliefs and you lose, it feels 10 times worse than just losing in a way where … if we lose doing it our way you accept it, take it on the chin and move on. It’s tough and it will still be tough.

“I’m so passionate about England and especially because I’ve been on this journey … been to finals, semi‑finals and been so close. Each one hurts in a different way and this one hurt, for sure, more than any other one. I’d say even more than when I missed the penalty in Qatar [in the 2-1 defeat by France in the 2022 World Cup quarter-finals] because of just the manner that it happened.”

It was put to Kane that it was a healing process. “It kind of is,” he replied. “But you have to heal while getting on with it. In football, you don’t have time. Before you know it’s the next one. It’s a hard balance because you’re trying to get over it and learn from it but also we play the world champions on Saturday and it’s a big, important game.”

Kane knows England must identify why they have repeatedly fallen short against the toughest teams when it matters most. “How can we be better in those moments? How can we be ourselves more in those moments? Through qualifying campaigns and a lot of games in tournaments, we play with a certain intensity, we play in a good way. It’s something that we haven’t quite been able to do in latter stages of tournaments against the bigger and better nations.

“It may be a mixture of things. It may be personalities, mentality. It may be just the direction and how we want to play in those games. It’s conversations that we need to have as a group.”

Kane accepts it was not only against Argentina that England were not at their best. “Taking away the big loss at the end, there were still games at the World Cup where we didn’t quite reach our potential, the way that we train,” he said.

But the message – as articulated by Thomas Tuchel when he addressed the squad at St George’s Park on Tuesday – was of the need to fine-tune. “The general messaging is that we continue what we’ve been building,” Kane said. “Sometimes after a tournament, it’s easy to say it’s a new start but I don’t think it is that. It’s a continuation because we have done a lot of good things.”

View image in fullscreen Harry Kane asked: ‘How can we be better in those moments? How can we be ourselves more?’ after England’s World Cup heartbreak. Photograph: Dylan Martinez/Reuters

Tuchel has been rocked by the withdrawals of Declan Rice, Cole Palmer, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento for the upcoming Nations League fixtures; after Spain, England play Czechia and Croatia away before returning to Wembley to face Czechia. Rice’s absence has attracted attention because it is for load-management reasons rather than an injury that would immediately rule him out. Kane understands the move, given Rice’s well-documented problems with nerve pain in a hamstring.

“I spoke to Dec,” Kane said. “I know Dec goes far and beyond for the club and country. I know he’s been struggling for a while with his issues. Dec reached out to me, he voice-noted me. Everyone has to look after themselves and I trust all the boys.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It is a seismic time for Kane. He is four caps shy of Peter Shilton’s all‑time England record of 125; he could be level with him by the end of this international window. Kane is also tipped to win the Ballon d’Or on 26 October and is poised to extend his contract at Bayern Munich. “We’re fairly close,” he said. “I’m happy there. It won’t be too long before there’s some sort of announcement.”

The 33-year-old allowed his thoughts to drift to the longer term and as he mused about his ambition to become an NFL kicker, there was a clear hint he saw himself finishing his football career in Major League Soccer.

“I take penalties and it [being an NFL kicker] is a very similar pressure and technique. If I was to do it, it is something I would take seriously. I would take six months to a year to try and practise before. Maybe if I am in the MLS in the future or somewhere like that, it might be a thing where you could connect the two maybe with the seasons.”

Kane has previously said he would be interested in becoming a professional golfer. He loves to play and revealed he did not watch the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina because he went for a round of golf in New York.

“I watch golf and think: ‘I could be there.’ Then I go out and play and I am like: ‘There’s no way.’ I play off two. But I am a member at Wentworth and I shoot 10 over. Then I watch the pros, who played there last week, and 20 under wins it. I think I’ll stick to football.”

Sports.title: Kaptein fantastic strikes as Chelsea battle to WCL win over Austria Vienna
Sports.content:
Wieke Kaptein’s early goal gave Chelsea a winning start to their Champions League campaign proper against Austria Vienna, but it was a far from comfortable evening for them.

“Probably the performance is not the one we wanted to have, we could have controlled the game a little bit better in terms of scoring a second goal to kill the opposition’s hope, but sometimes you need to focus on what is most important and tonight that was to win and to take the three points from the game,” said Chelsea’s manager, Sonia Bompastor.

A David v Goliath endeavour welcomed the visiting team at the Cherry Red Records Stadium and they rose to the challenge. The mammoth financial gulf between the two teams was highlighted by the Austrian broadcaster ORF in the buildup, who reported: “Chelsea Women’s personnel costs alone for the 2024-25 season, at a cool €17m, were higher than those of the entire Austria club (€14.9m) – including the men’s department, by far the largest item.” Meanwhile, Uefa noted that the manager, Stefan Kenesei, has a full-time job in state pensions insurance.

Ultimately, the gap in quality on the pitch looked far smaller than the finances suggested. Aware of that possibility, Bompastor did not take any risks and made only three changes to the team which earned a 2-0 win against Birmingham on Saturday, despite Arsenal up next on Sunday at Stamford Bridge.

It was a statement of intent from a team desperate to get their hands on the only club trophy to elude them and they were right to be cautious. As the Danish side HB Køge showed against Arsenal on Tuesday night, Champions League minnows can cause big problems.

“The physicality from those [lower-ranked] teams is good,” said Bompastor. “The players are able to match the intensity of the Champions League games from the beginning of the game until the end, as you could see tonight. I also think the coaches who are coaching those teams are good in terms of the tactical aspects. When they come into this game, they are really well prepared and they have a good game plan. So, nothing is easy.”

A moment of magic from the Dutch midfielder Wieke Kaptein gave the hosts the breathing space of an early lead 11 minutes in. The 21-year-old was quickest to the loose ball after a slick sliding tackle from Katharina Schiechtl dispossessed Melvine Malard and she sent a rising strike in off the underside of the bar from 25 yards.

Austria Vienna responded rather than folding, threatening until the final whistle while supported vocally by the small block of travelling fans who appreciated the efforts of the underdogs.

Quick Guide Roundup: Lyon hit eight, Barça rally past Paris FC Show Marie-Antoinette Katoto [pictured] scored a hat-trick as Lyonnes thrashed Servette 8-0 in their opening league phase game of the Women’s Champions League. Katoto’s treble, Melchie Dumornay’s double and two own goals from the Swiss hosts saw Lyonnes go top of the early standings with a crushing display. The eight-times winners went ahead eight minutes in through Laia Balleste’s own goal before Katoto took control. The France striker bagged her first of the night in the 28th minute and added a second 12 minutes later. Dumornay’s chipped finish gave Lyon a four-goal advantage at the break and just two minutes after the restart, Katoto completed her treble from Lily Yohanes' backheeled pass. Dumornay added her second in the 54th minute and Laura Strik’s own goal piled more misery on Swiss champions Servette, who conceded again in the 89th minute when Ines Benyahia struck. In Wednesday's other early kick-off, Roma substitute Marta Pandini hit the post with a stoppage-time penalty as they were held to a 0-0 draw at OH Leuven. Ewa Pajor’s double helped holders Barcelona get off to a winning start as they came back from behind to beat Paris FC 5-2. Barça were handed an initial scare when Evelyne Viens put Paris in front only five minutes in, but Kerolin replied for the hosts with a tidy finish in the 18th minute. Clara Serrajordi put Barca ahead 10 minutes later, kicking off a destructive 15 minute-period for the hosts, which saw Pajor and Caroline Graham Hansen strike. Pajor struck again in the 70th minute, before the visitors pulled one back through Clara Mateo as Barça comfortably saw out the win. Lyonnes host Chelsea next Wednesday in their second league-phase game, while Barcelona visit Roma and Paris FC welcome Arsenal. PA Media Photograph: Pierre Albouy/REUTERS Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Set pieces and the forward Modesta Uka were their best outlets. Uka’s close control provided both an attacking threat and gave her teammates a reprieve from chasing.

The threat from Uka had been evident in the Austrian side’s qualifying campaign. The Kosovan scored in their 3-2 win against Hajduk Split and scored another two in their 5-0 victory over Farul Constanta in the second qualifying round, before grabbing a hat-trick in a 4-0 win against the Norwegian side Brann to overturn a 2-1 away defeat in the third round and earn their place in the league phase.

“She’s a great player and she deserves to play at this level, just as the whole team does. She deserves to play in the Champions League and we’ve seen today how much potential there is,” said Kenesei.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The longer it went without Bompastor’s side building on their lead, the more confident the players in white became. Just shy of the 70-minute mark there was another tense moment for the hosts, when pressure from the ever-bright Uka forced Veerle Buurman into an error. Katie McCabe looked to have clipped the Austria Vienna player, who seemed to have beaten her to the ball, but a pause after the ball went out of play did not lead to an intervention from the video assistant referee.

View image in fullscreen Sonia Bompastor, the Chelsea manager, shouts instructions from the sidelines. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

Frustrations boiled over a little at the close, when Almedina Sisic re-entered the field without waiting a minute after receiving some treatment, with Bompastor forced to hold back her enraged assistant, Camille Abily, before giving the fourth official a piece of her mind.

In the end, it is a testament to the visiting team that they will leave London extremely disappointed not to have taken anything from a game that gave them opportunity after opportunity to do so.

“Yes, we’re proud. We were brave as we’d planned, really, but to be honest, I’m also disappointed that we didn’t get at least one point. We saw what you all saw today, that we performed at almost the same level as Chelsea,” said Kenesei.

Chelsea can breathe easy, although Keira Walsh’s withdrawal early on with a quad issue as a precaution will be a concern, but they have a job to do to snuff out those chances before they face teams that will capitalise and punish them.

Sports.title: Netherlands v Germany: Klopp and Xavi begin revival projects with derby
Sports.content:
Before the latest instalment of a time-honoured international rivalry gearing up for two distinct new beginnings, Jürgen Klopp could not resist sprinkling a little of the old mischief. “The good thing is that we both have the exact same situation,” he said of Xavi Hernández, his counterpart when Germany visit the Netherlands on Thursday night. “We met on Monday and play on Thursday. And the coach knows the players from television. I actually know more of the Dutch players personally than Xavi does. Whether that’s an advantage, I don’t know, but it’s still a fact.”

In his public appearances Klopp has been on irrepressible form since taking the role in July. The task of whipping Germany back into shape has visibly and audibly topped up the energy levels that had drained by the time he departed Liverpool. Klopp, his wit sharp and appetite piqued, looks a far cry from the character who, to most trained eyes, was going through the motions upon his unveiling as Red Bull’s head of global soccer early last year.

Securing Klopp was a coup for the German football federation even if it came with a caveat, issued within seconds of his introduction to the media, that he would not be seen for dust if his family were hounded by the media. Xavi’s arrival in Amsterdam is no less fascinating even if, in the Dutch way, no bones were made by his employers about the fact Pep Guardiola and Arne Slot had been higher in their sights after Ronald Koeman’s departure. He is the Netherlands’ first foreign manager since Ernst Happel’s 10-month stint ended in 1978 but the fit is instinctively pleasing. Even if Guardiola was out of reach, they could land upon another product of the Johan Cruyff school that created modern-day Barcelona.

View image in fullscreen Xavi’s captain is Virgil van Dijk, who considered international retirement after the World Cup. Photograph: Koen van Weel/ANP/AFP/Getty Images

If Xavi is to take the Netherlands, occasionally exciting but frequently unstable during a World Cup run that shuddered to a halt in the last 32, back to their roots it will require a measure of patience. The pool of players does not allow much else; the recall of Borussia Dortmund’s Joey Veerman, who has not played international football for more than two years, speaks of the need for a technically adept midfield fulcrum but otherwise Xavi has scant scope for surprises. Virgil van Dijk will continue as captain despite considering international retirement during the summer; the head coach’s options may feel more complete when Frenkie de Jong and Donyell Malen have returned from injury.

Xavi has resisted any temptation to engage in analysis of the Netherlands’ performance in the United States. “I don’t talk about the past,” is the standard line, ironically an easier one to roll out if the Nations League opener in Amsterdam brings a performance redolent of headier times. The revolution may have to be conducted with minimal effusive pronouncements from the coach. It is certainly a less dramatic shake-up than the one Klopp, acting like a man licensed to break a few moulds, has enacted before the next fortnight’s four-game baptism.

It raised eyebrows when Klopp named a squad of 44 players for the matches against the Netherlands, Serbia and, home and away, Greece. The expanded unit will be split into two: half will play on Thursday and in Germany’s next game, at home against the Greeks, and the remainder will be involved in the second two games. Only Finn Dahmen, the Augsburg goalkeeper, will be required across the set.

“I want to get to know as many players as possible,” Klopp said. “There is no A or B team. The squads are put together in a way that makes sense on the pitch and in terms of character and experience.”

View image in fullscreen The goalkeeper Finn Dahmen (centre) is the only player on call for all four Germany matches. Photograph: Federico Gambarini/DPA/AP

Club managers feeling squeamish at their players’ workloads during this expanded break will immediately have warmed to Klopp’s split selection. But the priority is to discover who best fits his vision for an intensely committed, front-footed, enthusiastic Nationalmannschaft that places round pegs, even unexpected ones, in round holes. Four players from Freiburg have made his sprawling selection; so has Felix Keidel from promoted Elversberg. Mika Baur of Celtic and the Hoffenheim winger Bambasé Conté were both stunned to receive first call-ups. The Brentford midfielder Vitaly Janelt joins his teammate Kevin Schade in the fray. Sixteen are uncapped.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Last weekend Klopp and his coaching staff convened at their headquarters in Herzogenaurach to watch as many of their charges’ domestic games as possible in one go. Freiburg’s Max Rosenfelder, one of the new brood, acknowledged the aura surrounding Klopp and described him as “a very, very special person”. Even if the mixed lineups prove to lack experience and cohesion, Klopp hopes his charges’ sheer thirst for the task will lift Germany from the doldrums of their most recent World Cup flop.

If he can unite 44 players, why not a whole country? Among Klopp’s many recent pronouncements was the timely intervention in favour of “positive patriotism” that followed an election victory by the anti‑immigration Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) party in Saxony‑Anhalt. If it is some time since Germany’s football team have been at their best, perhaps the same may be said for the nation too.

In the Dutch capital, two big‑name managers will take their first steps towards bringing the good times back. “It could be a bit wild, but I accept that, it just has to be lively,” Klopp said. That comes with something approaching a cast‑iron guarantee.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo vows to play on for Portugal and targets 1,000 career goals
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo said he considered quitting international football after the World Cup, but confirmed he plans to play on for Portugal and hopes to reach 1,000 goals for club and country. Ronaldo, who is 21 goals shy of the milestone, accepted some critics are trying to “kill” him but is determined to carry on.

Ronaldo, who has won 233 caps for his country, captained Portugal in the summer at the World Cup, where they exited to Spain in the last 16. Asked if he considered walking away from international duty, he replied: “Yes, I did. Of course, I’m always thinking about my decisions, my future, the present also. I’m a thinker; you have to think. This is why you see me here now, it means I will continue.

“I had a conversation with our president [Pedro Proença], with our coach. I still believe that I’m able to help the national team to reach what they want. I think I can give the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football. There is a new young generation, but for me the basic point is to be able on the pitch to score the goals and to help the team win games.

“Whenever they say they don’t want me in the national team, I will be the first one to go. When I think I am not adding anything to the team, or that I create an atmosphere, I will be the first to go. I will take my suitcase and leave. The Portuguese count on me. That’s why I’m still here … Just look at the numbers, I’m sure you can make some calculations, I’m still doing well. The day they don’t count on me, no problemo, I will leave. I will always be the No 1 fan of this federation.”

Jorge Jesus, the Portugal head coach who managed Ronaldo at Al-Nassr, said the 41-year-old would start in his first game in charge, against Wales in the Nations League on Thursday. Jesus, who has succeeded Roberto Martínez, also launched a passionate defence of Ronaldo, drawing applause from many in attendance at Portugal’s City of Football complex in Lisbon.

Quick Guide Bellamy remembers 'president' Ronaldo's arrival Show Craig Bellamy said Wales must enjoy facing “heavyweight” opposition in Portugal on Thursday and colourfully recalled being stuck at Lisbon airport because it was on lockdown to ensure Cristiano Ronaldo a “president-like” arrival. Bellamy (pictured) twice visited the city on pre-season camps with Burnley, where he worked as assistant to Vincent Kompany for two years. “He is beyond a superstar,” the Wales manager said of the Portugal captain, whom he shared a pitch with in the Premier League almost 18 years ago, when Ronaldo, who turns 42 in February, scored twice in a 2-0 win for Manchester United at home to West Ham. “There were rows of police cars everywhere,” Bellamy said of the moment he realised the airport was on lockdown. “We were like: ‘Something’s happened. We thought it was a security breach. We were stuck on the coach for about 10, 15 minutes. ‘When are we going to get off the coach?’ Suddenly this car turns up – I’ll be doing it a disservice but it was a Bentley or something like that – and parks in this parking slot, this guy walks out the front, goes to the boot, grabs this rucksack, and this other kid comes out the front, puts the rucksack on. Who is it? Ronaldo. “Even the police are like [trying to look at Ronaldo] but no one could bother him. It was the coolest walk I’ve ever watched. For a minute, we were on the coach just jaws dropped. ‘Everyone who is moaning? Shut up.’ We don’t mind. We’re watching this … it was like president stuff. How can you lock off a whole airport? I won’t even be able to get my computer through customs at Cardiff. What have I just seen?” Bellamy was effusive in his praise for Portugal’s all-time record goalscorer, who is closing on 1,000 goals for club and country. “Who gets 1,000 goals?” the 47-year-old said. “Seriously? It’s just silly, eh? I hope he gets it – but I hope he gets nothing on Thursday. We’re talking about one of the greatest players of all generations – his name will go down in history for hundreds and hundreds of years.” Ben Fisher Photograph: José Sena Goulão/LUSA Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“Cristiano is a symbol of Portugal and the national team,” said Jesus, sitting alongside Ronaldo at the Portugal federation’s campus. “If he will play the games, he is not entitled to that, it is up to the manager to decide.”

Ronaldo cut a relaxed figure on stage alongside Jesus. “For me the most important thing is I know what I am,” he said. “I know what I do to be here, I know what I have done to have the success that I have had. I know why young kids love Cristiano, because they see me as an example, and I will continue to do that. Even when I am retired … in 10 years.

“I’m happy with myself. It doesn’t matter if I play tomorrow, if I’m rested for the next game, for me the most important thing is that I feel good. The people around me, they trust in my work. Focus on the people who love Cristiano, not the people who criticise me, so I am a happy person.”

Asked directly about the criticism, Ronaldo triggered laughter from many in the room by replying: “I cannot be 100% honest, sometimes I have to be politically correct.” He added: “I do understand that some TV channels like to criticise me, they’ve tried to kill me – with a shotgun – but I can still move away from it. Anyway, I am used to it. I have been doing this for more than 20 years, I’m quite used to it. What I can control, I will. What I can’t, I won’t.”

View image in fullscreen Cristiano Ronaldo attends a training session before the Nations League group stage match against Wales. Photograph: Rodrigo Antunes/EPA

On Thursday Ronaldo will return to the Estadio José Alvalade, where he began his career with Sporting, before joining Manchester United in 2003. It is Portugal’s first game in Lisbon since beating the Republic of Ireland in a World Cup qualifier last October.

“It’s a special feeling because it was there where my beautiful history started,” Ronaldo said. “I’m very proud about that, to play for the national team after so many years, playing where I practically was opened to the world … It was a beautiful moment.

“It is always a pleasure to play for the national team, to wear the colours of Portugal. After so many years, it is [still always] like the first time. I will step on to the pitch with passion, emotion. I hope we can get off on the right foot. Because it’s at Sporting, it does feel a bit more special.

“It would be the cherry on the top of the cake to score my 1,000th goal with the national team. It would be the culmination of a beautiful story. I said I wanted to reach that target and I will reach that target. But I don’t have an obsession. If you are obsessed with something, you won’t get it … Just enjoy. Carpe diem, enjoy the day.”

Sports.title: Christian Eriksen leaves Wolfsburg by mutual consent after on-pitch collapse in June
Sports.content:
Christian Eriksen and the German side VfL Wolfsburg have agreed to terminate ⁠his contract by mutual consent, the club announced on Wednesday.

The 34-year-old collapsed during a Denmark friendly ⁠against Ukraine in June. Eriksen said in July he would ​return to his homeland to undergo a ‌rehabilitation programme. He previously suffered a cardiac arrest during Denmark’s opening Euro 2020 group match ⁠against Finland in Copenhagen in 2021.

The decision brings ⁠an early end ⁠to ​Eriksen’s contract, which was set to run until June 2027. The midfielder joined Wolfsburg as a free agent a year ago, making 34 appearances across all competitions. Eriksen scored three goals and provided 10 assists for the Wolves, but could not prevent their relegation from the Bundesliga.

“At the moment, it is important for me to ‌be close to my family in Denmark. I’m pleased that we were able to find a solution together,” Eriksen said in a statement. “My time in Wolfsburg was marked by many highs and lows,” he added. “I know that the club is now ‌in good hands as it aims to make its way back to the Bundesliga, and I am convinced ​that a successful future lies ahead for VfL.”

The Wolfsburg ⁠managing director of sport, Dieter Hecking, said the second-tier club granted ​Eriksen’s request to ​cancel the agreement. His last appearance for the team came in May’s promotion/relegation playoff defeat by Paderborn.

“He has already ​experienced and achieved a great deal during his ​extraordinary career,” ‌Hecking said. “Despite his ​short time ​here, he has left a lasting impression on his teammates, our staff and the fans.”

Eriksen played for Ajax, Tottenham and Inter before his on-pitch collapse in 2021. He was fitted with an implantable cardioverter-­defibrillator (ICD) device, but had to leave Inter because Serie A rules prohibit playing with a pacemaker.

View image in fullscreen Denmark and Ukraine players gather around Christian Eriksen after his collapse in June. Photograph: Bo Amstrup/Ritzau Scanpix Foto/AP

After joining Brentford in 2022, Eriksen spent three years at Manchester United before joining Wolfsburg last summer. He said in June that his ICD device “did what it was designed to do” after he collapsed on the pitch for a second time.

“Receiving a shock from my ICD has had a major impact on both me and my family, but I want to reassure everyone that this was a different situation from what happened in 2021,” Eriksen posted on social media.

“I am feeling good, and my recovery has already started. I am incredibly grateful to the doctors who have cared for me and my heart over the years. Thanks to their expertise, my ICD did exactly what it was designed to do: protect me when I needed it.”

Sports.title: Manchester United report seventh straight annual loss and sell fans £125 grass clumps
Sports.content:
Manchester United have reported an annual loss for the seventh ­successive year, taking the club’s combined losses to £444m since 2019.

The financial results were released as it emerged United are raising revenue by selling small clumps of grass from the Old Trafford pitch to supporters. United relaid the playing surface for the first time in 14 years this summer, and an email to fans has offered them the chance to buy 7cm x 7cm clumps of turf for £125.

The £43m net loss for 2025-26 is a significant increase on the £33m for the previous 12 months, with compensation paid to the sacked manager Ruben Amorim a contributory factor along with the decision to increase the club’s borrowing facility by £93m to help fund the redevelopment of Old Trafford.

United’s continued losses come despite record revenue of £677.6m – up 1.7% on the previous 12 months – and the implementation of a major cost-cutting regime by Sir Jim Ratcliffe under which hundreds of staff have lost their jobs.

In discussing United’s results on an investor call, the chief executive, Omar Berrada, said the club’s summer transfer window, during which they spent £155m on three players, had been planned with “financial sustainability in mind” in an indication that the budget will continue to be tight for newthe manager, Michael Carrick.

That is underlined by the fact that United’s wage bill dropped to £301m, down 3.6% on the previous year, more than £100m lower than Manchester City’s.

While United reported operating profits of £22.6m for the 12 months to 30 June 2026 the increase in revenue was more than offset by the cost of financing the club. Net finance costs more than tripled to £69.2m from £21.2m in the previous year, partly owing to foreign-exchange ­movements, and the club refinanced several loans, increasing their net debt from £471.9m to £577.6m.

United sources have said the refinancing provided funding for the £63.5m purchase of a plot of land next to Old Trafford required to build their proposed new 100,000 capacity stadium, the first major investment in a complex project that could end up costing more than £2bn.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Berrada said the results demonstrated “the underlying strength of our business, particularly in a season without European football” and said: “This shows the direct impact of the work we have been doing over the past two years. It also proves Manchester United’s enduring popularity and commercial strength. While these results confirm that we are on the right trajectory, we will continue to take a disciplined approach to ensure our finances remain sustainable.”

United are confident their financial outlook will improve over the next 12 months owing to the club’s return to the Champions League and the start of increased sponsorship deals with the training-kit partner Betway and shirt-sleeve partner SumUp, which will bring in £20m and £22m a year respectively. The club is forecasting revenue of between £740m and £760m for 2026-27.

Sports.title: Ireland manager gets prime minister Martin’s backing in row with Israel over ‘genocide’
Sports.content:
Ireland’s prime minister, Micheál Martin, backed his country’s football manager, Heimir Hallgrímsson, after Israel’s football federation accused Hallgrimsson of “stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy” over comments about the war in Gaza.

“I think those are unacceptable remarks; they should be withdrawn,” Martin told reporters in New York, where he is attending the UN general assembly. “Israel can’t keep denying what the world knows, and what the world understands.”

Hallgrímsson sparked the row after saying before two Nations League fixtures against Israel: “We’re not playing with genocide, we’re playing against genocide. We’re playing against Israel, we’re not playing with Israel.”

Quick Guide How do I 

Martin said Hallgrímsson’s comments reflected concerns about the scale of death and destruction in Gaza, also citing remarks by the UN secretary general, António Guterres.

On Wednesday Hallgrímsson, preparing for Thursday’s game in Kosovo, expressed gratitude for Martin’s backing. “What I said at the last press meeting has taken the attention away from maybe what’s most important; we are playing an important game against Kosovo,” Hallgrimsson said.

“Maybe, from a ‌leadership point of view, not clever for me to take the attention like this. But to answer the question, we are thankful for all the support we get. It’s a tricky time for ​us.“

The dispute comes amid mounting controversy in the Republic over the fixtures, scheduled for 27 September and 4 October. More than 160 Irish sportspeople have signed an open letter calling on the national team to boycott the matches, and protesters gathered outside the team’s Dublin hotel on Monday. Further protests are planned around the country in the run-up to the games.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) passed a motion last November requesting that European football governing body, Uefa, suspend Israel from international competition. The FAI has said it has little choice but to fulfil the fixtures or risk sporting and financial sanctions.

Ireland’s designated home match on 4 October was moved from Dublin’s Aviva Stadium to Backa Topola, Serbia, after concerns over disruption and security. The 27 September match, officially Israel’s home fixture, will also be played at a neutral venue, in Debrecen, Hungary.

Israel strongly rejects allegations that its conduct in Gaza amounts to genocide. Hamas led the deadliest attack against Israel on 7 October 2023 when militants killed 1,221 people and dragged into Gaza 251 hostages, 44 of them already dead, according to Israeli official figures.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Sport in Focus Our picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown in Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Israel launched a massive retaliatory offensive that has displaced virtually the entire population at least once and has killed 73,919 people, according to the Gaza health ministry, which operates under Hamas and whose figures are generally considered reliable.

Ireland has long been a strong supporter of the Palestinian cause, with sympathy for Palestinians often linked to the country’s history of British rule. Dublin formally recognised a Palestinian state in 2024 alongside Spain and Norway and has repeatedly criticised Israel’s conduct of the war in Gaza.

Reuters contributed to this report

Sports.title: Man United reveal how much money they've SAVED with sacked boss Ruben Amorim taking over at AC Milan - as they try to rake in more cash by selling bits of the pitch for £125!
Sports.content:
Manchester United saved £8.5million when Ruben Amorim took over as head coach of AC Milan, the club’s latest financial results have revealed. United reported in May that the total compensation due to Amorim and his staff could rise to a maximum of £16.7m. But his appointment as Milan boss in June meant United have paid £8.2m, less than half that figure. Wednesday’s results also revealed that the cost of financing United’s debt has now rocketed past the £1billion mark since the Glazer family’s leveraged takeover. The club’s annual figures show that United paid £69.6m – an increase of £48.4m or 228.3 per cent from the previous year – in interest and other finance costs. The overall debt itself still stands at more than £1bn despite the cost-cutting measures imposed by minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos which contributed to United turning a £18.4m operating loss into a £22.6m over the last year. It consists of £577.6m of historic debt from the Glazer takeover in 2005, £111.4m owing on the club’s revolving credit facility and outstanding transfer fees. Ineos co-owned Man United have announced record revenue of £677.6m for the 2025-26 season The Americans’ £790m buyout has been the biggest factor in United bleeding over £1bn in the last two decades, and that infuriates fans who are fiercely opposed to the Glazers’ ownership and increasingly disillusioned with the Ratcliffe regime. After spending just £163m in the transfer market this summer – substantially less than many of their rivals – United are 12th in the Premier League table after one win in five games. The club are also at odds with large sections of the fanbase over their attempts to increase revenue and, more recently, crack down on ticket touts. It has also emerged that emails have been sent out to members and season ticket holders offering them the chance to buy miniature squares of the Old Trafford turf – which was re-laid in the summer for the first time in 14 years – for £125. United laid a new playing surface at the 'Theatre of Dreams' for the first time in 14 years over the summer, and the old pitch has been cut into 7cm x 7cm squares. Those squares have been packaged in acrylic cubes and are being sent out to supporters who want them in a smart black casing. The United website reads: 'Take home a piece of Old Trafford with this official turf cube, perfect for fans who want a keepsake from one of the most famous pitches in the world. 'Carefully preserved, this piece of turf makes a priceless memento of iconic games played at home and keeps the memories of match days alive. The sacking of Ruben Amorim in January cost the club £8.5million in compensation 'Perfect for gifting to passionate Reds, this turf cube makes a great addition to desks or can be displayed in a cabinet with other Manchester United collectibles.' The club have described the purchasable turf as a 'one-of-a-kind collector’s item' to club members and season-ticket holders in an email offering them 'exclusive' early access. Despite the huge debt and costs of servicing it, United are still committed to building a new £2bn stadium. The latest financial results revealed that the club spent £63.5m in June on a 25-acre triangle of land located 350 metres away from Old Trafford. While United were able to announce record revenues of £677.6m despite not playing in Europe last season, they reported an overall net loss of £43m – up from £33m last year – which sources say demonstrates the importance of maintaining financial discipline. Chief executive Omar Berrada said: ‘We are pleased to have secured record revenues which demonstrates the underlying strength of our business, particularly in a season without European football. United are selling small cubes of last season's Old Trafford turf to fans for £125 ‘This shows the direct impact of the work we have been doing over the past two years. It also proves Manchester United’s enduring popularity and commercial strength. ‘While these results confirm that we are on the right trajectory, we will continue to take a disciplined approach to ensure our finances remain sustainable.’ Commercial revenue for the year was down £16m and sponsorship revenue by £27.9m, partly due to United having no training kit sponsor following the end of their partnership with Tezos. The club have since signed a record £20m-a-year deal with Betway, as well as replacing sleeve sponsor DXC Technology with SumUp. Retail & merchandising revenue for the year was up £11.9m, and broadcasting revenue by £33.9m due to United finishing third in the Premier League after Michael Carrick replaced Amorim in January. Matchday revenue was down £6.8m due to the club’s shortest season since the First World War. Not playing in Europe and going out of both domestic cup competitions at the first hurdle meant that United played just 40 games.

Sports.title: Essex cricket star charged with two counts of rape
Sports.content:
Essex cricket star charged with two counts of rape

The Essex cricketer Robin Das has been charged with two counts of rape and will appear at London Crown Court on Friday, October 9.

Das, 24, was arrested in August last year following allegations of a woman being raped in Brixton in March 2024.

A spokesman for the Metropolitan Police said: 'Robin Das of Queens Road, Waltham Forest, was charged on 23 July 2026 with two counts of rape.

'The charges follow his arrest on 27 August 2025 following reports of a woman being raped in Brixton on 30 March 2024. The woman continues to be supported by specialist officers.'

Das, predominantly a batsman, made his debut for Essex in 2020 and has gone on to make over 60 appearances for the county in all formats. His only senior game this season was in a One-Day Cup match against Middlesex on July 21.

He has been suspended since being charged two days after that match.

Robin Das has played over 60 games for Essex since making his debut in 2020

Essex CC said in their statement: 'Essex County Cricket Club can confirm that a male member of the playing staff, currently under contract with the club, recently appeared in court in relation to an incident that took place outside club activities.

'Throughout, the club has remained in contact with the ECB, PCA, the Cricket Regulator and the player with regard to the matter, which included an immediate and ongoing suspension. The club will continue to follow all appropriate legal processes and guidance.

'As a club we have strict safeguarding and HR procedures in place, and all employees of Essex County Cricket Club are required to meet the highest standards of professional conduct at all times.

'As legal proceedings are in progress, the club are unable to make any further comment at this time.'

Sports.title: PREMIER LEAGUE REPORT CARD - PART ONE: Arsenal begin the defence of their crown, Brighton and Brentford are the surprise standouts and faltering Fulham remain winless - so what grades will they get?
Sports.content:
PREMIER LEAGUE REPORT CARD - PART ONE: Arsenal begin the defence of their crown, Brighton and Brentford are the surprise standouts and faltering Fulham remain winless - so what grades will they get?

The international break is upon us, calling a brief halt to a thrilling new Premier League campaign. The first five weeks have seen a flood of goals, plenty of upsets and many contentious moments.

With that in mind, Daily Mail Sport have compiled report cards for all 20 sides so far. Here are the first ten to go under analysis....

ARSENAL

Position: 2nd. Points: 12

As expected the reigning champions hit the ground running proving early on that they will be hard to dethrone by earning four wins from five.

The Gunners picked up where they left off last season, beginning the campaign with an emphatic 3-0 home win against newly promoted Coventry to set the tone for their first title defence in 22 years.

Since the opening day, Mikel Arteta's men have won a number of extremely testing fixtures. The Gunners claimed three points away at Aston Villa, who have caused them trouble in previous seasons, as well as beating London rivals Chelsea at home and winning at the ever hostile Stadium of Light where big money signing Bruno Guimaraes scored his first goal for the club.

But it has not been a flawless start for Arsenal as they endured a miserable afternoon on the south coast losing 3-0 to Brighton – the first time they have failed to score in a Premier League game since January.

Nevertheless the Gunners still look formidable and are poised to challenge for the title again and perhaps seek the European glory they missed out on in Budapest in May.

Grade: A-

Despite a small blip Arsenal's start indicates they will be tough to dethrone and are after more silverware this time around

ASTON VILLA

Position: 16th. Points: 4

After a standout season last year where they finished fourth and won the Europa League, the Villains have not carried their excellent form from last season into this.

Unai Emery, now in his fifth season at Villa Park, has been unable to get his new-look side to tick yet despite some promising signs. Villa started the season on a whimper losing 4-0 at the hands of Brighton, conceding all four goals in the first 31 minutes of the game.

Since their opening day thrashing, Villa have lost to both Arsenal and midlands rivals Nottingham Forest, while they failed to score against new boys Hull in a bore draw.

Villa can be somewhat excused for a slow start with this season being a slight transition year for the club after losing several key players over the summer including their two top scorers Ollie Watkins and Morgan Rogers as well as star centre-half Ezri Konsa. But even the most pessimistic of supporters would not have envisaged a start such as this.

They did manage to pick up their first three points of the season just before the break in a well-deserved 3-2 victory away at Tottenham and beat Club Brugge away from home in their Champions League opener. Big money signings Nicolas Jackson and Johan Manzambi have also looked to be finding their feet in the side.

After the first five games Villa sit two places from the drop, and will need Emery to mastermind a turnaround in form quickly if this season is to end with more success.

Grade: C-

Unai Emery has worked wonders during his time at Villa Park but how will he manage this transition?

BOURNEMOUTH

Position: 17th. Points: 3

Another side that overperformed last season and have not been able to keep up the pace is Bournemouth, with the Cherries winless under new manager Marco Rose going into the international break.

Bournemouth seem to have suffered the same fate many mid-table sides do when playing in Europe as they won their first ever European bout away at Real Sociedad but are yet to get off the mark in the Premier League.

The South Coast side managed their highest ever finish in English football last season by placing sixth, only three points off the Champions League places, and did very well to hold onto to almost all of their top talents in the summer.

But the Cherries have clearly had one very costly loss with head coach Andoni Iraola upping sticks for Liverpool. His replacement Marco Rose arrived with a glittering resume having coached some of Germany's biggest sides but has yet to realise his vision at the Vitality.

A harsh run of fixtures have made this a tough first month of the season for Bournemouth, having to face Man City, Liverpool and Newcastle already, but there is no excuse for not winning a single game yet and the pressure will be on Rose and his side to deliver when they return.

Grade: D

Bournemouth will have to pick up form quick if they want to avoid a spiral into a relegation scrap

BRENTFORD

Position: 4th. Points: 9

From one extreme to the other Brentford have been marvellous in their opening fixtures as Keith Andrews continues to prove people wrong with his high-octane pressing machine churning out results every week.

As one of five unbeaten teams, the Bees are buzzing with two wins and three draws to kick off the season.

A strong transfer window saw Brentford hold onto key players, including Caoimhin Kelleher and Igor Thiago, and add some excellent young players which has helped create a free-scoring team that looks so hard to beat.

The 3-0 drubbings of Chelsea and Tottenham demonstrated the lethal nature of this Brentford attack, with five of the six total goals coming in one half of each game.

Three score draws in between these two London derbies leaves them in contention for a sustained European push.

Grade: A

Brentford look ready to push to new heights this season after thrashing rivals Chelsea and Spurs at home

BRIGHTON

Position: 3rd. Points: 10

Brighton have enjoyed a dream start to the season with Fabian Hurzeler having orchestrated some truly excellent performances. His free-scoring side have netted a whopping 16 goals in their opening five games, more than any other side in the top flight.

The Seagulls kicked off with a bang beating Aston Villa 4-0 at home and have since enjoyed victories over Coventry and champions Arsenal, keeping clean sheets against both. Hurzeler's men have dropped points to Chelsea and Leeds in-between but were then buoyed by a magnificent Carabao Cup comeback victory over Manchester United.

Brighton as always had an excellent window and it shows, with new boys Malick Yalcouye, Chema Andres and Luka Vuskovic having already impressed. The Seagulls were particularly brilliant in beating Arsenal through a patient defensive approach that forced the champions to play long and lose possession constantly.

Questions will be asked about Brighton's ability to maintain this style of play over the course of 38 games, with the added strain of European football, but their performances have certainly shaken up the Premier League and it will be fascinating to see how their season unfolds.

Grade: A

The Seagulls are flying! Brighton are becoming a dreaded fixture after a blistering, goal heavy start to the season

CHELSEA

Position: 10th. Points: 7

To the surprise of many who tipped Chelsea to be fighting for the title the Blues have been remarkably inconsistent in their opening games.

After another whirlwind summer that saw Chelsea bring in Xabi Alonso as head coach and sign 11 new players, it looked as if they had finally plugged the gaps in their squad and were ready to seriously challenge – especially when playing only one game a week.

The Blues have instead looked as unstable as ever, conceding more goals than any other side so far (12) and picking up one point from their last available nine. It is not all bad news at Stamford Bridge as summer signing Morgan Rogers has looked electric and has become the final piece of a fearsome front three alongside Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro. But the midfield has looked barren without Moises Caicedo and the defence looks calamitous.

It is clear that Alonso intends to outscore opponents this season at the expense of clean sheets but currently his side are just shipping goals and cannot score enough to pick up wins. Chelsea won their opening two matches against Fulham and Brighton in exciting fashion but since have dropped points to Hull and lost London derbies to Arsenal and Brentford.

Sat exactly in the middle of the table, Chelsea are already in danger of another disappointing season unless Alonso can find a balance in his squad and find consistency.

Grade: C-

Free scoring Chelsea will need to sort out their defensive woes if they are to avoid another disappointing season

COVENTRY CITY

Position: 18th Points: 3

The first of the new boys to receive their grade is Frank Lampard's Championship winners Coventry City. After a 25-year absence from the Premier League the Sky Blues will have one objective for this season: survival.

Anticipation for Coventry's first Premier League season in over two and a half decades was sky high in the summer but their start has been woeful.

The new boys tasted defeat in their first four games without scoring. Lampard struggled to bring in proven Premier League talent over the summer and it has shown in his team's performances.

They were handed some unfortunate early fixtures having to play both Arsenal and Manchester City in their first three games, but losing at home to Hull in-between those two games is a real cause for concern. Brighton's 5-0 demolition at the Building Society Arena has left some believing Coventry are condemned within the first month.

They managed to breathe some life into their survival hopes at midlands rivals Nottingham Forest with an impressive 1-0 victory thanks to a beautiful Jay DaSilva goal but they will need a lot more if they are to get out and stay out of the bottom three.

Grade: C-

Lampard got Coventry into the top flight but this will be the Premier League legend's biggest test yet

CRYSTAL PALACE

Position: 15th. Points: 4

For some Palace fans the international break will come as a welcome respite after a hectic summer and stressful start to the season.

A new manager, new defence and new beginnings in the Europa League promised a chaotic season and it has delivered so far. One win in five is cause for concern but Eagles fans must be patient and allow the squad to adapt to new manager Pierre Sage's system.

Similarly to their west London rivals Chelsea, Palace have had no problem scoring but are struggling to keep opposing teams out at the other end, conceding 11 goals already. A loss to newly promoted Ipswich has prompted suggestions the Eagles could slip into a relegation scrap if they are not careful.

The Europa League has provided a welcome distraction and their hope for back-to-back European trophies was inflated by a rampant 4-0 win over Lech Poznan in their opener.

All in all Palace seem to be par for the course, their form suggests a slight but not urgent worry for relegation and an exciting opportunity in the Europa League where they have nothing to lose but everything to gain.

Grade: C+

Crystal Palace have been free scoring at one end but unable to keep opponents out at the other

EVERTON

Position: 7th. Points: 9

After a disappointing end to their first season at the eye-catching Hill Dickinson Stadium veteran boss David Moyes has the Toffees looking sweet again.

Everton remain unbeaten and look solid all over the pitch. Thierno Barry seems to finally be coming good, Dewsbury-Hall has built on last season's impressive showing and Jack Grealish has given this side an extra injection of flair and quality.

One of their key strengths has been late goals, equalising in stoppage time against both Bournemouth and Manchester United as well as getting their winner against Wolves in the Carabao Cup with ten minutes left on the clock.

With Tyrique George looking a real threat and Tyler Dibling showing signs of wanting to join the party, there is every chance for Moyes to get the club back into Europe.

Grade: A

Prime Minister's vote: Andy Burnham was cheering on the Toffees during their Carabao Cup victory over Wolves

FULHAM

Position: 19th Points: 2

It has been a truly disastrous start to the campaign for the Cottagers, who remain winless with pressure already being piled on new boss Alvaro Arbeloa.

Fulham took risks in the summer with decision to appoint Arbeloa and back him with several young inexperienced talents from Real Madrid's B team, but it has yet to pay off so far.

After draws in their last two games Fulham will be desperate to finally pick up three points upon return from the international break

The existing squad appear unable or unwilling to adapt to the Spaniard's style of play and are conceding terrible goals at one end and appearing panicked up the other. New boys Shea Charles, Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios all seem to be talented young players but their inexperience is ultimately hindering their new team.

This is Fulham's worst ever start to a Premier League season and for the first time since their return to the division in 2022 the Cottagers are a relegation worry.

Arbeloa will need to start finding form and fast, the international break will give the players a much-needed rest and give the coach some time which he must use wisely.

Grade: E

Sports.title: Revealed: Jurgen Klopp's list of four rules for Germany's stars in his first managerial job since leaving Liverpool - with WAGs told to stay away, barbers BANNED and new professional standards
Sports.content:
Revealed: Jurgen Klopp's list of four rules for Germany's stars in his first managerial job since leaving Liverpool - with WAGs told to stay away, barbers BANNED and new professional standards

Jurgen Klopp has reportedly introduced four rules for Germany stars as the former Liverpool boss seeks to turn around the fortunes of their national team.

Klopp will take charge of Germany for the first time on Thursday when they face the Netherlands in the Nations League, after being unveiled as the new national team boss back in July.

The 59-year-old, who took the job after a two-year break from the dugout, will hope to restore Germany’s standing after a decade of underperformance at international tournaments.

Klopp succeeded Julian Nagelsmann after Germany crashed out of the World Cup to Paraguay in the last-32, with the presence of players’ WAGs and families placed under the spotlight in the aftermath.

Nagelsmann's partner also made headlines, with German media reporting that his girlfriend, Lena Wurzenberger, was an almost constant presence in the camp.

According to German newspaper Bild, Klopp has sought to significantly restrict their presence as one of four rules for his squad to follow in Germany’s new era.

Jurgen Klopp has introduced four rules for his Germany squad as part of their new era

Players' wives and girlfriends will have limited access during training camps and tournaments

The presence of players' families around the camp was a major talking point during Germany's underwhelming World Cup campaign

The Germany head coach will no longer permit ‘team outings’ during tournaments, which had enabled players’ entire families to visit the team’s headquarters throughout the last World Cup.

Instead, Klopp will reportedly allow families to visit on a limited basis, with the intention that players are able to fully focus on their common goal during training camps and at Euro 2028.

Players have also been banned from being visited by hairdressers at Germany’s team accommodation, with stars instead having to have their hair cut prior to the camp as part of an aim to introduce new professional standards.

Klopp is also reported to have stressed that players must be present for dinner promptly at 7pm or 8pm, rather than arriving gradually, in a move aimed at giving players more time to socialise and connect with each other.

A focus has been placed on encouraging conversations between players in an attempt to grow team unity, including during gym sessions and massages.

As part of the drive, Klopp has banned the use of mobile phones at these times, as well as on matchdays, ensuring his side are focused on essentials in the build-up to their matches.

The rules aimed at improving team culture come with Germany seeking to transform their performances at major tournaments.

Germany have made three consecutive early exits since winning the World Cup in 2014, with group stage eliminations in 2018 and 2022 before a last-32 exit this year.

Klopp has reportedly banned mobile phones at certain times and is encouraging players to socialise more together in an attempt to build team spirit

The national team were also eliminated in the last-16 and quarter-finals of the past two European Championships, with their last semi-final coming back in 2016.

Klopp will assess a 44-man split squad in the first matches of his reign, with the players used across four Nations League fixtures.

The unusually large squad is being separated into two to handle an extended three-week international break, as they face Netherlands, Greece and Serbia.

Klopp has already clashed with German media after his squad selection was leaked earlier this month, while in his first press conference he threatened to resign if his family faces any scrutiny.

After his first game as Germany boss on Thursday, Klopp's side will then take on Greece for the first of two clashes just three days later.

The former Liverpool boss will then switch to his second squad for a clash with Serbia on October 1 before they play Greece again on October 4.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo reveals he considered RETIRING from Portugal duty after the World Cup as he opens up on pursuit of 1,000 career goals
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo reveals he considered RETIRING from Portugal duty after the World Cup as he opens up on pursuit of 1,000 career goals

Cristiano Ronaldo has confirmed he considered retiring from international duty after the World Cup but stressed he will 'always be available' to help the Portuguese national team.

Ronaldo, 41, had refused to confirm whether he would continue representing Portugal after his fifth and final World Cup in the summer, where the national team suffered a limp 1-0 defeat in the last-16 to eventual champions Spain.

Despite the expectation that Ronaldo would retire from international football, the forward was named in new manager Jorge Jesus's first 25-man squad for their upcoming Nations League matches against Wales, Denmark and Norway.

Speaking ahead of their opening match with Wales, Ronaldo admitted he nearly called time on his career with the national team.

'Yes, I'm always thinking about my decisions, I think about everything. You see me here, so I decided to continue,' Ronaldo said at a press conference.

'I still believe that I'm able to help the national team to reach what they want. I think I can give the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football.

Cristiano Ronaldo has admitted he considered retiring from international football this summer

Ronaldo, 41, had been non-committal over his future with Portugal after their World Cup exit

'There is a new young generation, but for me the basic point is to be able on the pitch to score the goals and to help the team win games.

'Whenever they say they don't want me in the national team, I will be the first one to go. When I think I am not adding anything to the team, or that I create an atmosphere, I will be the first to go. I will take my suitcase and leave.

'The Portuguese count on me, that's why I'm still here, just look at the numbers, I'm sure you can make some calculations, I'm still doing well.

'The day they don't count on me, no problem, I will leave. I will always be the No 1 fan of this federation.'

Ronaldo insisted he is only focused on the 'present moment' after being asked whether he would be continuing until next summer – when the Nations League finals will take place – or until the 2028 European Championships.

He acknowledged there are critics that 'try to kill me' but said he is motivated by people who still want to keep seeing him play.

'I cannot be 100 per cent honest, sometimes I have to be politically correct,' Ronaldo said.

'I do understand that some TV channels like to criticise me, they've tried to kill me – with a shotgun – but I can still move away from it.

Ronaldo acknowledged reaching 1,000 career goals was a target but said it is not an obsession

'I am used to it, I have been doing this for more than 20 years, I'm quite used to it. What I can control, I will. What I can't, I won't.'

The Al-Nassr forward, who has scored 146 goals in 233 games for Portugal, was questioned about his desire to reach the 1,000 career goal mark.

Ronaldo, who is 21 goals short of the staggering milestone, declared that while it was a target he was not obsessed by it.

'It would be the cherry on the top of the cake to score my 1,000th goal with the national team. It would be the culmination of a beautiful story.

'I said I wanted to reach that target and I will reach that target. But I don't have an obsession. If you are obsessed with something, you won't get it.'

Jesus confirmed Ronaldo will start against Wales on Thursday, with the new boss describing the veteran forward as 'a symbol of Portugal'.

Sports.title: Harry Kane reveals Declan Rice sent him a voice note explaining his absence as he sends warning to England's five drop-outs - and insists stars will hold inquest over Argentina defeat
Sports.content:
Harry Kane believes England’s five World Cup drop-outs are losing out on vital preparation time for the 2028 European Championships. Kane is no stranger to the matter of players withdrawing from England camps. In November 2024 the England captain delivered a resolute message to the nine players who had declared themselves unavailable through injury for the final two games of Lee Carsley’s spell as interim coach. ‘I think England comes before anything,’ said Kane back then. ‘England comes before club.’ Almost two years on, Thomas Tuchel’s first England squad following the World Cup will be missing Arsenal’s Declan Rice and Cole Palmer of Chelsea – who played 90 minutes for their clubs at the weekend – as well as Manchester United duo Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo and Newcastle full-back Tino Livramento. Kane said: ‘We spend so much time at club level together and building on the pitch, off the pitch. You don't get that luxury with international football. ‘So, for me, personally, just every moment together [matters], every camp together, just to get to know players, get to know how people play tactically, how the manager wants us to play. Harry Kane and Lewis Hall compete for the ball in training at St George's Park ‘All these things are really important as before we know it, we will be in the summer and then we will be in the Euros in 2028. ‘It seems we are far away from the Euros, we're far away from Nations League final next summer, but we're not. 'We have two weeks now, we have a week in November. We have a week or so in March, and then we’re hopefully playing a Nations League semi-final and final in June, and then it's the same next season. ‘So, although it seems far away, I think actually it’s not a long time at all.’ Two years ago, Kane accused his missing team mates of taking advantage of an opportunity to essentially have a break. This time he didn’t go anywhere near as far. 'I've spoken about this before and I don't want to make it a big thing,’ said Kane. ‘Everyone has their own situation. I know how tough the summer was and I know especially in the Premier League how gruelling that schedule is. ‘I trust all the boys. I spoke to Dec, for example. He sent me a voice note. I know Dec goes far and beyond for the club and country, so I know how much he gives and I know he's been struggling for a while with his issues. Declan Rice is sitting out England's four Nations League fixtures amid what Kane described as a 'gruelling' Premier League schedule ‘From our point of view, I think the togetherness that we have will not be shaken through people not being here right now. All it does is give other people opportunity to impress the manager.’ Kane is 33 now and will match Peter Shilton’s England appearance record of 125 if he plays in all four games against Spain, Croatia and Czechia (twice) over the next fortnight. Sitting in his training gear at St George’s Park today, the Bayern Munich striker looked in the shape of his life, something underlined by his status as one of the Ballon d’Or favourites ahead of the ceremony in London next month. Mentally, however, the scars of an ultimately disappointing World Cup are taking longer to heal. Kane revealed that he chose not to watch the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina, flying to New York to play golf as soon as England’s third-place play-off win had been secured against France the day before. In his mind, questions remain unanswered. The most pertinent one revolves around the way that England played in defeat to Argentina in their semi-final in Atlanta. ‘This one hurt for sure more than any other one,’ said Kane. Kane admitted the defeat by Argentina hurt more than any other in his career ‘I'd say even more than when I missed the penalty against France in Qatar because of the manner in which it happened. ‘It felt like it wasn't us as a team out there. It wasn't the team that we wanted to be and said we'd be. ‘I think sometimes when you maybe go against your beliefs and you lose, it feels 10 times worse than just losing doing it your way and accepting it and taking it on the chin and moving on.’ England’s retreat to their own penalty box after taking the lead against Argentina is something that continues to vex England supporters and indeed their coach. As such, it felt natural to ask Kane why it happened. ‘I think those are the questions that we need to kind of discuss amongst ourselves and answer ourselves, as players and as coaching staff,’ said Kane. ‘How can we be better in those moments? How can we be ourselves more in those moments? Through qualifying campaigns and a lot of games in tournaments, we play with a certain intensity and we play in in a good way. ‘It's something that we haven't quite been able to do in latter stages of tournaments against the bigger nations and the better nations and it may be a mixture of things. It may be personalities. It may be mentality. It may be just the direction and how we want to play in those games. ‘But I think it’s a conversation that we need to have as a group. We wanna try and take that next step because I think that would be an important one.’ England’s 24-man squad – Tuchel has replaced two of the missing group with Everton’s James Garner and Nottingham Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White – gathered at their Staffordshire base on Monday and immediately sat down for a briefing with the head coach. Thomas Tuchel is ready for the next phase of his time as England boss having fallen short in the World Cup semi-final Tuchel’s public reflections on seven weeks in America last Friday were fascinating without ever being consistently enlightening. But it’s clear from what he said to his players this week that he has identified problems transferring training performances to matchday familiar to a series of England managers who have passed before. Kane revealed: ‘I think it's trying to translate how well we train into games. ‘It’s easier said than done, but if we can get better at that I think we'll show an even better version of ourselves. So that was kind of the general meeting really. ‘We're still going to talk about the summer and talk about good and bad. That will happen naturally over the next year. ‘We have to heal while getting on with it. In life in general, whenever there's like big major events, you have time to process it, you have time to talk about it. ‘In football, you don't have that. In football, before you know it's the next one, and now we're focused on Nations League. ‘So it's a hard balance because you're trying to get over it and learn from it. But also we play the world champions on Saturday and it's a big, important game.’
