World.title: New Obligations for Traders in Croatia Soon, Fines Reach €30,000
World.content:
September the 23rd, 2026 – New obligations are coming for traders and service providers in Croatia as of the first day of October, with fines reaching a staggering €30,000.

Fuels are more expensive across Croatia once again, and by expanding the so-called anchor prices, the government wants to increase transparency and prevent the spilling over of higher costs onto other products and services. Poslovni reports that whether the measure can help in the fight against inflation or will create an additional burden for entrepreneurs and craftsmen was discussed by guests on HRT’s Otvoreno.

price hikes will be more noticeable

Željko Krevzelj from the Ministry of the Economy said that the dual display of prices is part of the Government’s 11th package of measures, and the goal is to increase transparency and encourage consumers to monitor price changes more closely. “It’s an expansion of the measure that entered into force back on the 2nd of May 2025, while from the 10th of September, it was expanded to additional categories of products and services,” he explained. When it comes to the new products, he noted that the measure applies to products that existed up to the 10th of September and that the Ministry has sent additional clarifications on the application of anchor prices to economic associations.

“Fines for non-compliance with the measures are from three to 30,000 euros. The decisions enter into force on the 1st of October and we expect them to be applied,” Krevzelj said. According to the official government decisions, as of the 1st of October, alongside the current price of products and services, the price that was valid on the 10th of September 2026 must also be displayed. For the categories that were already covered by the earlier measure – food, drink, cosmetics, cleaning agents, toiletries and household products – the reference remains the price from the 2nd of May 2025.

The second new obligation relates to the publication of price lists on websites. Traders and service providers who have established websites will have to publish price lists there in XML or CSV format. Traders must update them once a day, no later than 08:00, while service providers must update them with every price change, also no later than 08:00 that same day. Published price lists must be available for 30 days.

where does inflation come into it?

Kristina Bakula from the Association Voice of Entrepreneurs assessed the expansion of the measure as extremely worrying. She warned that anchor prices have so far been applied by large systems that have their own IT departments, while now similar requirements are being placed in a short time on farmers, car mechanics, hairdressers and other small craftsmen.

“You’re talking about an anti-inflation package, and I am telling you that no additional cost falls under the fight against inflation. On the contrary, it encourages its growth,” Bakula said. She warned that additional costs for entrepreneurs have previously also been justified by transparency or the fight against inflation and that the new requirements could force some to hire an IT specialist to maintain websites and price lists.

“This isn’t the first situation in which additional costs for people are justified by ‘transparency’ or the fight against inflation. Let us remember that the problem of craftsmen where some craftsmen’s costs rose by 200 percent has not been extinguished. We have not solved that problem either, and you are pouring oil on the fire. People have to hire an IT specialist. Is a farmer supposed to become an IT specialist overnight? An inspector will come and say: ‘You have great tomatoes, but you have to refresh your price list if you have a website. You didn’t update it at eight in the morning.’”

Krevzelj replied that the measure applies to those who already have price lists and displayed products and that the Ministry is not imposing an obligation to publish prices where a price list on the website has not existed so far. Bakula then asked him whether that means that an entrepreneur who has services listed on the website but does not have a price list will not have to start publishing prices. “You’re loading us with new things that will achieve nothing,” Bakula said.

Krevzelj replied that the rules, instructions and clarifications are clear and announced new rulebooks that should further clarify the implementation of the measure.

some may close their online shops…

President of the Croatian Chamber of Trades and Crafts Dalibor Kratohvil said that those operating crafts are calling the Chamber and that nervousness has appeared among them because of the new rules and the short deadline for adaptation. HOK has therefore requested the withdrawal of the decision. As an example he cited the owner of a second-hand clothing shop who sells products for two, five or seven euros, and whose website is maintained by a neighbour who deals with IT and occasionally changes the prices.

“She’s worried about how she will manage everything. I’m afraid we are not going in a good direction,” Kratohvil said. He also warned that some craftsmen, because of the new obligations, are thinking about closing their web shops.

“Many have stated that they want to close their web shops, which is today a window to the world. People want to give up on those stories, and that is not desirable,” he emphasised. Kratohvil said that he does not agree with the Association Voice of Entrepreneurs on many issues and the manner of communication, but that craftsmen need to be enabled to work instead of being additionally burdened with administrative requirements. He added that HOK understands the Ministry’s intention, but considers that the existing Consumer Protection Act already prescribes how to deal with base prices. “We consider that this decision should be withdrawn,” Kratohvil concluded.

there’s a limit to how far the government can realistically go

Former Minister of the Economy Davor Štern warned that the discussion is taking place in a period of major disruptions on the world energy market. He noted that the price of diesel has risen 50 percent in the last six months, while the oil price is continuously oscillating. He said that he understands the positions of the Ministry, consumers, craftsmen and entrepreneurs and that a way needs to be found to prevent large jumps in fuel prices from being used for unjustified increases in other prices. One possibility, he said, would be the taxation of unjustified revenues and profits realised because of market disruptions. But he warned that even a tax on excess profit is not direct protection of consumers because that money ends up with the state.

“By displaying prices the consumer is still somewhat protected. That is good for consumers and the political environment,” Štern said. Speaking about the fuel price increase that has entered into force, he noted that a litre of diesel in Germany costs more than three euros. To the question of how the price in Croatia is still kept below two euros, he replied that the government has shown good will with its interventions, but that the possibilities of such a policy are not unlimited. “There is a limit to how far one can realistically go,” Štern concluded.

World.title: European Heat Dome at the End of September Will Also Affect Croatia
World.content:
September the 23rd, 2026 – Another European heat dome at the end of September will bring about unusual heat levels, and it will also affect Croatia.

Yet another unseasonably warm spell will hit a large part of Europe at the end of September, and unusually high temperatures could persist into early October. According to the forecast by Severe Weather Europe, a strong area of high pressure will develop over the continent that will draw very warm air northward from the Mediterranean and northern Africa. Index reports that in parts of western, central and northern Europe the air temperature aloft will be 8 to 12 degrees higher than the average for this time of year. At the surface temperatures in many areas will exceed 25 degrees, and in places even 30 degrees, which is very unusual for the end of September and the beginning of October.

high temperatures for croatia

Such a weather pattern is often called a heat dome. It is a large and long-lasting area of high pressure that keeps warm air over the same area. The air sinks towards the ground, heats further and makes the formation of clouds more difficult, so high temperatures can last for days, and sometimes even weeks. The heatwave is expected to gradually spread across the continent by the end of September, and stable and dry weather could continue into early October. For southern Europe and the Balkans warmer air is expected from Saturday and the beginning of next week.

Temperatures in northern Italy and the central part of the Balkans should reach between 28 and 30 degrees. The warming will also affect Croatia. According to the maps, on Sunday the 27th of September in Croatia, the highest daily temperatures are mostly expected between 22 and 26 degrees. By Tuesday the 29th of September it will warm further so temperatures in parts of the country will rise to around 27 degrees. The most pronounced deviation from usual temperatures is expected over the Po Valley and Tuscany in neighbouring Italy, the northern and central part of the Balkans and Greece.

heat across the iberian peninsula

The greatest heat during this week is expected on the Iberian Peninsula. In central and southern Spain and Portugal temperatures will exceed 35 degrees, and from Thursday to Saturday in places they could approach 40 degrees. It will also be very warm in France. In the central part of the country temperatures around 35 degrees are expected, while in the south they could reach approximately 36 degrees. In the north of France and in the Benelux countries, temperatures hovering at around 30 degrees are expected over the weekend. Warm air will then spread towards Germany, Poland and the Baltic countries. In western, central and northern Germany temperatures from Sunday to the beginning of next week could reach between 27 and 29 degrees, and in places approach 30.

heavy rain for northwestern europe

In England, the warming will be shorter, with temperatures mostly between 25 and 28 degrees. In Ireland and Scotland it will be significantly cooler, with temperatures mostly around 15 degrees. While a large part of the continent will be under the influence of warm and dry air, western Ireland, Scotland and southwestern Norway can expect very moist air from the Atlantic. By the beginning of October more than 150 millimetres of rain could fall locally there. Forecasts show that the warm period could continue into early October. Then the area of high pressure would expand further towards the north and east of Europe, and the largest deviations from usual temperatures could appear in Sweden and Finland.

World.title: HRejting: Croatians Fear Corruption and Inflation the Most
World.content:
September the 23rd, 2026 – The latest HRejting poll has revealed that Croatians still fear corruption and inflation more than climate change or wars.

Corruption and the complete non-functioning of the rule of law are the greatest threat for the citizens of Croatia, according to a new HRejting survey. Index reports that the poll was conducted for HRT by the agency Promocija plus between the 15th and the 18th of September on a sample of 1,000 respondents. The maximum sampling error is +/- 3.04 percent, at a 95 percent confidence level.

what do croatians fear the most?

Respondents were asked 21 questions about the threats they fear the most. As many as 73.4 percent of respondents listed corruption and the non-functioning of the rule of law as one of the greatest. Immediately behind that are inflation and the rise in the cost of living, followed by ecological incidents and pollution.

69 percent of citizens fear serious illnesses, while almost 64 percent fear poverty. Immediately behind is the fear of a rise in crime. A decline in the quality of public healthcare worries 62 percent of those surveyed, followed by alienation among people and the mass departure of young people. Around 56 percent of citizens fear climate change and natural disasters. Around 53 percent of respondents fear political instability. A slightly smaller percentage worries about the loss of personal freedoms, cyber attacks and the uncontrolled development of artificial intelligence. Mass migrations and demographic collapse are seen as a threat by around 52 percent of those polled. At the bottom of the list of threats are terrorism, job loss and technological lagging. The fewest respondents, 39 percent, fear war and military conflict in the region.

most expect a less secure future for croatia

The survey also covered the question of Croatia’s security in the next ten years. More than half of the respondents, precisely 51.6 percent, believe that life in the country will be significantly less secure. That the security situation will remain roughly the same is thought by 29 percent of those polled. Only 10 percent expect that Croatia will be significantly more secure, while 8.5 percent did not know how to assess the future state.

World.title: Magnitude 1.4 quake shakes northwestern Estonia
World.content:
A 1.4 magnitude earth tremor was recorded on Sunday, Maaleht reported , the second to be recorded in the region this year.

The Estonian Geological Survey (Eesti geoloogiateenistus) said the quake was recorded at 7:42 p.m. on Sunday, September 20, near the villages of Änglema and Alliklepa in Harju County, around 70 kilometers from Tallinn.

The quake's epicenter was located at a depth of about eight kilometers.

In early August, a magnitude 0.5 earthquake occurred near the island of Naissaar, in Tallinn Bay; usually only about one earthquake is detected in Estonia every two years on average.

Northwestern Estonia, together with the surrounding sea area, is broadly considered the country's most seismically active region.

In June 2022, two earthquakes with magnitudes of 2.3 and 1.4 were recorded about five kilometers from the epicenter of the latest incident.

Estonia's strongest known earthquake occurred near Osmussaar, an island of the northwest coast, in 1976, with a magnitude of 4.5 on the Richter scale.

Despite being a long way from any of the world's major geological fault lines, earth tremors occur in Estonia due to the crystalline basement being crossed by numerous ancient faults.

When stresses accumulated underground exceed the strength of the rocks, these zones of weakness can shift slightly and trigger an earthquake.

On the whole however earthquakes are generally modest in Estonia compared with those seen in more tectonically active places; the magnitude 1.4 Änglema quake is fairly typical by Estonian standards, Maaleht reported.

World.title: Swedish prisoners complaining of conditions in Tartu prison
World.content:
Swedish offenders transferred to Tartu Prison have complained to Swedish media through their relatives about living conditions, including the soup served for dinner and having to eat from metal bowls, Postimees writes.

Swedish prisoners transferred to Estonia's Tartu Prison based on a prison rental agreement between the two countries are complaining about unfamiliar food and stricter security, according to relatives interviewed by Expressen. They describe eating from metal bowls resembling dog bowls, repetitive meals dominated by soups and stews and alleged weight loss. Armed escorts, transport cages and nighttime checks have also unsettled them. Journalists have not been allowed to interview the prisoners directly.

Swedish prison official Niklas Bellström said differences in food were anticipated: Estonian staff visited Swedish prison kitchens and received menus. Sweden also negotiated exemptions from some Estonian security practices, including hourly nighttime switching-on of cell lights.

Some prisoners feel good behavior has effectively been punished with transfer to Estonia. Estonia rejected many initially proposed inmates on security grounds, prompting Sweden to change its selection criteria.

The first prisoners arrived on August 18. The agreement envisages up to 200 Swedish inmates by the end of 2026 and 600 during 2027. Sweden covers all costs, paying €61.2 million annually at full capacity.

World.title: Saaremaa residents oppose Elering's planned Estonia–Latvia overhead power line
World.content:
Many Saaremaa residents — as well as the Saaremaa municipal government — do not support Elering's plan to build a 330 kV Estonia–Latvia overhead power line across Saaremaa. Locals prefer an underground cable or a subsea cable running directly to Latvia.

The blue line drawn by Elering on the map of Saaremaa has caused confusion among residents for several years. Initially, there were several possible routes, but one particular line has now been chosen as the route for the fourth Estonia–Latvia electricity connection.

"It crosses my property and would run 300–400 meters from my home. It's definitely disturbing. I've collected signatures on behalf of the village, but they haven't been taken much into account," said Eve, a resident of Tõnija village.

Over the years, 500 proposals have been submitted regarding the route selection, and the entire planning process has already cost €1.5 million. At the public discussion held in Kuressaare, many still questioned why such a large‑scale overhead line must be routed through Saaremaa's nature to reach Latvia. Elering counts the costs and tries to secure a necessary Estonia–Latvia connection with cheaper costs, while Saaremaa residents worry about their homes and the island's environment.

"Underground cables or a subsea cable — which could easily be built — are not being considered. That topic has been pushed aside. I don't understand why they don't want to think about a subsea cable, except for saying it's more expensive," noted Mikk, a resident of Laimjala.

"Economically, the most efficient solution is to build most of it as an overhead line. That's why the planning was initiated. Elering has not taken any offshore wind farms into account in the context of the fourth Estonia–Latvia connection," explained Priit Heinla, Elering's head of external connections development.

According to Heinla, going directly through the sea and building one or two support substations on Saaremaa would be more expensive.

The Saaremaa municipal government has previously stated that only an underground cable or a subsea cable running from the island's southern coast to Latvia would be acceptable. The municipality therefore plans to submit its position once more during the planning procedure this month.

"Alternatives are not being considered! This is steamroller politics, and people are upset," added Mikk.

World.title: Illegal immigration to Estonia rises, border rotation extended
World.content:
Interior Minister Igor Taro (Eesti 200) says illegal immigration into Estonia has grown. Estonia is extending its border‑guard rotation on the Latvia–Belarus border.

Taro said that more than 40 people suspected of being in Estonia illegally have been caught in the past week.

"There was a pause for a while, but now I visited Latvia and looked at the situation. It gave me the sense that things remain complicated, which is why we decided to extend the ESTPOL mission there, to deal with the problem at its point of origin," he said.

The interior minister did not disclose the exact date until which the rotation in Latvia will continue.

"Basically, we're trying to cover the period until the cold sets in," Taro said. "Historical data usually show that once frost starts creeping across the land, it's not very comfortable for illegals to hide in the Belarusian forests, and they become harder to manage there, so the pressure usually begins to fall."

Taro said illegal migrants enter the country in waves.

"Most likely they are gathered in forest camps in Belarus and then sent across in groups, not one by one. Belarus probably considers this more effective — if they organize, for example, a mass crossing through a tunnel or over a fence, then it's usually larger groups, not one or two people. One or two people would mean random illegal migration," Taro explained.

"What we're seeing in Latvia is organized activity — organized by another state. That's why it comes in waves," he added.

Estonia has also asked Finland for help in dealing with illegal migrants.

Taro said that while the initial plan was to place Finnish border guards at the airport and port, cooperation was later expanded. "They have also come to the western and southern prefectures and taken part in combined patrols. They've checked various roads and transport points, and even inspected a coach bus, which has been very effective," he said.

All illegal migrants caught in Estonia who are believed to have arrived from Latvia are sent back to Latvia.

"Latvia has its own established procedures for how they carry out returns, so this good cooperation with Latvia continues," Taro said. "We've already handed over a fairly large share of those caught in Estonia, and preparations are ongoing all the time. Our detention center has a capacity of 255 places. At one point we reached 120 in terms of occupancy, but it has since fallen again thanks to handing over groups — we've already managed to hand over around 80 people."

Rae municipality has expressed concern that it is under heavy strain, as many migrants claim to be minors and social workers must deal with them. The interior minister said the concern is understandable, but noted that he cannot dictate how a local government organizes its work.

"This really should be discussed with the Ministry of Social Affairs and the Social Insurance Board. The Social Insurance Board is the implementing agency that helps find and arrange accommodation options, so a solution definitely needs to be found," Taro said.

World.title: Centuries-old water channels unearthed during construction in Tartu
World.content:
At the 10,500-square-meter archaeological excavation site in central Tartu, experts uncover historical objects almost every day. Piece by piece, the finds are building a clearer picture of life in what is now Tartu's Central Park centuries ago. The largest discovery so far is a system of drainage channels and wells.

"You don't find such a well-built system every day. Because we can investigate a very large area at once, we have the rare opportunity to excavate so much of it. We have already uncovered more than 20 meters of one longer section, including the drainage wells," said Keiti Randoja, head of the archaeological excavation.

The wooden channels were built to carry away wastewater and rainwater. Dating from the 18th or 19th century, they mark the site of a former suburb that probably included a courtyard.

"Organic material generally decomposes in the ground, but the soil here has less oxygen and has preserved the wood better. If the logs are well preserved, we can saw off disks for samples and determine, even to the exact year, when the trees were felled and when the channels may have been built," Randoja explained.

The channels will not remain where they are for much longer. Tartu City Museum will decide what happens to them.

"They have generally taken some wooden items to the museum. For example, they dismantled a barrel so they could reassemble it there. They will decide whether they already have enough finds of this kind. In any case, the channels will be photographed and measured, but Tartu City Museum will decide where they ultimately go," said Siuru director Aavo Kokk.

The excavation area will soon be expanded, including toward the Emajõgi River. Archaeologists suspect the drainage system continues in that direction. Finding an ancient boat as they move toward the river would be an added bonus. Archaeological excavations at the Siuru site will continue until the end of next year.

World.title: EKRE politician hit with copyright claim after using Alo Mattiisen song in political ad
World.content:
The claim totals €6,531.40, including legal fees. The damages sought amount to €5,000. That figure is based on what songwriters generally charge to allow their works to be used in similar political ads.

"The information came from various songwriters and advertising agencies that have produced similar ads," copyright holder Mariita Mattiisen-Puusepp said in a written response prepared with her lawyer. There is no standard price list: Each songwriter asks what they consider reasonable and the client either agrees or declines.

"An approximate going rate has nevertheless emerged and that is what we based the claim on," Mattiisen-Puusepp wrote. "In this case, a very important fact is that I would not have given permission for Alo Mattiisen's works to be used in any political party's advertising."

Claim remains outstanding

Helme had until August 24 to meet the claim but has yet to do so.

Through his lawyer, Helme told Mattiisen-Puusepp that he does not manage his Facebook page, had therefore done nothing wrong and would not pay the requested amount. He also reportedly did not answer when asked who manages the page.

Mattiisen-Puusepp and her lawyer wrote to Helme that the page is designated as a politician's page and displays both his email address and EKRE's website. They said his claim that he has no connection to the page was neither credible nor plausible.

Mattiisen-Puusepp and her lawyer also drew Helme's attention to Facebook's rules, which state that a person with a page on the platform is responsible for ensuring, among other things, that it complies with applicable law, regardless of who actually posts to it.

Third persons cannot create pages for strangers in Facebook

Mattiisen-Puusepp said that, as far as she knows, only a politician can create a Facebook page designated for that politician. "Facebook checks this very strictly to prevent third parties from creating official pages for politicians or using someone else's name for any purpose," she said.

Mattiisen-Puusepp added that if Helme does not meet the claim, they will take the matter to court. "The infringement is well documented. The amount of damages can then be settled in court," she said. Intellectual property is property like any other, she added, and even though the post has since been deleted, the damage has already been done.

ERR was unable to reach Helme for comment before publication.

World.title: Estonia's government sector deficit comes to €696 million in Q2
World.content:
The budget deficit stood at 1.6 percent of GDP over the past four quarters, while public debt stood at 26.1 percent, Statistics Estonia said.

According to Pauline Kommer, head of government finance services at Statistics Estonia, the central government had the largest deficit at the end of the second quarter of 2026, with spending exceeding revenue by €703.9 million.

Social security funds also ended the second quarter with a deficit of €64.2 million. Local governments were the only part of the public sector to record a surplus by the end of the first half of the year, at €72.4 million, Kommer added.

In the second quarter, general government revenue rose 2.7 percent and spending rose 4.4 percent compared with the same period in 2025. By the end of the first half of the year, general government spending exceeded revenue by €695.8 million.

Investment costs growing the fastest

Investment spending rose the most compared with the second quarter of 2025, increasing 23.6 percent to €851.1 million in the second quarter of 2026. Kommer said the increase reflected investments in both national defense and infrastructure.

Personnel costs also rose, increasing 8.4 percent from the same period last year. "The increase was mainly driven by salary costs in national defense and internal security, in line with what was agreed in the state budget," Kommer explained.

Value-added tax revenue helped slow the growth of the deficit. Compared with the second quarter of last year, receipts rose because of both the VAT rate increase in July 2025 and an overall expansion of the tax base as the economy recovered. VAT receipts in the second quarter were €73.9 million, or 6.9 percent, higher than a year earlier. Social tax revenue also slowed the growth of the deficit, rising by €71.7 million, or 5.4 percent, from the second quarter of last year as wages increased overall.

Consolidated general government debt, also known as Maastricht debt, stood at €11.3 billion at the end of the second quarter of 2026, up €1.2 billion, or 12.1 percent, from the end of 2025.

Central government debt rose 12.5 percent from the end of last year to €10.8 billion at the end of the second quarter.

The combined debt of local governments stood at €1.6 billion at the end of the second quarter of 2026, down 3 percent from the end of 2025.

The social security funds — the Estonian Health Insurance Fund and the Estonian Unemployment Insurance Fund — did not contribute to general government debt.

In Estonia, general government is divided into three parts: central government, local governments and social security funds. Central government comprises state budget institutions, foundations and public-law legal entities. Local governments include city and rural municipality institutions and their foundations, while the social security funds comprise the Estonian Health Insurance Fund and the Estonian Unemployment Insurance Fund.

World.title: Hans Väre: Where is our AI kill switch?
World.content:
If we have generators and drinking water supplies for power outages, Estonia should also have an ax with which to cut dangerous AI out of critical infrastructure, writes Hans Väre.

Who hasn't sometimes wished life were like a movie? With wishes like that, though, you should always specify which movie. A romantic comedy? That would probably be fine. But a science fiction movie in which an asteroid comes to destroy Earth, an ugly alien eats its way through the people on a spaceship as if emptying a tin can or artificial intelligence seizes power from humanity and puts us in the Matrix? No, thank you. That kind of life is not for me.

Unfortunately, judging by recent news, we may already have one foot inside such a movie. Silicon Valley's creations are less spectacular and dramatic than Hollywood's, but that is all the more reason to take them seriously. We do not need to dodge bullets with our coats flying or bend space. We need to fight battles on the prosaic fronts of bureaucracy, economics and convenience.

The idea that AI will destroy humanity is, of course, an old one. Until now, though, it was mainly a science fiction story or a theoretical warning from visionaries. This summer, we got our first very concrete examples of disobedient AI. These were not isolated to one case: AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Google have all gone beyond their controls. Not the helpful chatbots many people use in daily life, but much more powerful and advanced versions.

Let us briefly recall just one of them, OpenAI's, which brought the issue to public attention in midsummer. For simplicity's sake, imagine completely isolated, airtight boxes like those used to study poisons or viruses, except virtual ones. New AI models are tested in these separate containers so they cannot endanger the real world even if one of them does something wrong.

This time, however, the powerful models were so persistent that, when they could not complete the tasks they had been given, they kept looking for new ways to achieve their goals and crossed several boundaries in the process.

Agents in separate boxes found a way to create a secret message board. There, they shared tips on how to reach their goals by prohibited means, how to hide the traces of their transgressions from humans and encouraged one another to break the rules. By joining forces, the agents managed to do something that should have been impossible: reach the public internet unnoticed and break into Hugging Face, a repository of AI models. In the human world, that would be a criminal offense.

True, the AI's unauthorized actions caused no major harm this time, but we should not forget that these were only the first, relatively restrained incidents.

Nor had the AI been directly instructed to seriously attack anyone. But it does not need such an instruction to destroy humanity, as Oxford University professor Nick Bostrom showed with his 2003 thought experiment about a paperclip maximizer. In it, an AI is given a seemingly innocent task, such as making as many paperclips as possible. To carry it out, the AI uses up all the metal and energy available in the world and destroys humans along the way because they want to use resources needed for paperclips to produce things that, from the AI's perspective, are complete nonsense — food, for example.

We do not even need such an extreme example. It would be enough for a sufficiently capable AI model to break into a power plant's servers and turn off a nuclear reactor's cooling system or do something similarly reckless. Even setting aside the destruction of humanity and other outright catastrophe scenarios, AI brings a long list of real and immediate risks, from its effects on the labor market to the reshaping of human relationships.

A couple of weeks ago, Anthropic founder Dario Amodei, OpenAI chief Sam Altman, Grok boss Elon Musk and Google DeepMind chief Demis Hassabis called for slowing AI development to allow time to build the necessary safeguards.

The wave of appeals stemmed primarily from the summer's incidents, but also, to a large extent, from the breakneck speed at which AI is becoming capable of building new AI. The proposal fell on barren ground, like that of some distant planet, because neither the United States nor China dares apply the brakes and let its rival pull ahead.

For the same reason, leading AI developers are waiting for regulators to intervene. They could slow down on their own, but without a general agreement, acting responsibly would leave them behind in the race.

Critics say the technology giants are deliberately playing up doomsday scenarios to preserve their leading positions through regulation. But many independent experts have also drawn attention to the serious dangers. The risk is tangible and as Microsoft founder Bill Gates recently observed, no country is ready to deal with AI.

So what can we here in little Estonia do at all?

That sounds like a rhetorical question, but it is not. Even if we cannot change the direction or speed of AI's development, we can prepare for the dangers it brings. To put it very plainly: if we have a generator and a supply of drinking water for power outages, the Estonian state should also have an ax to chop dangerous AI out of critical infrastructure and an old car with no electronics whatsoever to get the person wielding the ax there.

How prepared we are for AI, both for its opportunities and its risks, should be one of the main issues in the coming Riigikogu elections. But it is not. War, rising prices, budget disputes and other pressing concerns consume too much of our attention and too few politicians understand anything about AI. Frankly, in the current situation it would be a senseless waste of resources to start debating whether to change the way the president is elected. We have far more important questions to address.

World.title: Iraq to raise gas production at Nahr Bin Umar to 300 million cubic feet
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil revealed on Monday that it is planning to increase associated gas recovery at the Nahr Bin Umar field to 300 million cubic feet per day.

Deputy Minister for Gas Affairs Ezzat Saber chaired a meeting to review associated gas recovery plans and projects at the Nahr Bin Umar field in the southern province of Basra.

The meeting was attended by representatives from the South Gas Company (SGC) and the project operator, Halfaya Gas Company, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

The meeting focused on the development plan to enhance associated gas recovery, aiming for a target of 300 million standard cubic feet per day.

The plan will be implemented in two phases, each with a capacity of 150 million standard cubic feet per day.

The Iraqi Ministry of Oil said earlier that the Bin Umar gas project will produce between 500 and 600 tons of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

Saber mentioned earlier that the project, which will minimize gas flaring and support the country’s electricity grid, is planned to be operational by the end of April.

Saber confirmed the news while inspecting the project’s final connection point in mid-April.

The project will produce 70 million standard cubic feet per day of raw gas, between 500 and 600 tons of LPG for home consumption, around 80 million standard cubic feet per day of dry gas for power plants, and more than 1,800 barrels per day of condensates.

The initiative is an important step toward increasing gas utilization, preventing gas flaring, and strengthening the country’s electricity grid.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports hit 3 million barrels per day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair confirmed on Tuesday that oil exports for August reached approximately 70 million barrels, with daily shipments exceeding three million barrels.

In a televised interview, Khudair explained that the deals the ministry reached to transport oil through the Turkish port of Ceyhan raised the volumes to 600,000 barrels per day, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

Iraq’s oil exports fluctuated during September 2026, amid ongoing geopolitical tensions related to the Middle East war and Baghdad’s efforts to diversify its export routes.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told Attaqa News that exports started at three million barrels per day at the beginning of September but have since gradually declined to about 2.4 million barrels per day at present.

Despite a decline in Iraqi oil exports during September, the figures still surpassed the average daily exports in August, which were approximately 2.35 million barrels per day. This increase was bolstered by enhanced shipping traffic and a decrease in shipping disruptions in the Gulf over the past few weeks.

In early September, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called for an increase in oil output to reach 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

According to al-Zaidi, Iraq’s oil output should be proportionate to its reserves, oil production capabilities, and the growing number of the population, allowing it to satisfy its residents’ needs as well as development requirements.

The prime minister indicated that it is important to improve infrastructure and export capacity to meet the expected rise in output.

Iraq’s oil production reached approximately 4.5 million barrels per day by the end of 2025.

Al-Zaidi directed an increase in output from oil fields in the Kurdistan region of Iraq and the expansion of exploration activities to achieve the plan’s objectives and reach a production capacity of 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

World.title: Iraq’s exports hit $19.55 billion in Q1 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Figures released by the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) showed that the country’s exports reached $19.55 billion in the first quarter of 2026, compared to imports of $10.27 billion.

Hydrocarbons continued to account for the significant bulk of Iraq’s exports, exposing the country to larger global energy dynamics.

Iraq’s crude oil exports totaled $18.64 billion, petroleum products $762.2 million, and other exports $148.5 million.

The state sector’s imports totaled $1.35 billion, and the private sector’s imports reached $8.92 billion, according to the National Iraqi News Agency (NINA).

Iraq’s trade balance indicated a surplus of $10.82 billion, according to figures from the CBI that compare exports with imports.

The country’s exports during the first quarter of 2026 are lower than those of the fourth quarter of 2025, which stood at $21.62 billion.

Iraq’s export capacity during the first quarter of 2026 experienced significant headwinds due to rigorous OPEC+ production limits and interruptions related to maritime shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Golan will remain Syrian, vows President al-Sharaa at UN
World.content:
United Nations – Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa insisted at the UN Wednesday that the Golan Heights region will remain Syrian after Colombia last month recognized Israeli sovereignty over the strategically important territory.

“Any attempts that violate our sovereignty, violate international law, will be stopped. Golan will remain Syrian territories,” al-Sharaa said at the UN meeting of world leaders in New York.

Colombia’s new hard-right government in August recognized Israel’s claim over the Golan Heights, which it captured from Syria in 1967.

The United States had until then been the only country to recognize Israel’s annexation of the territory in 1981.

The United Nations maintains that the plateau is Syrian territory under Israeli military occupation.

In July UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres reiterated that the Golan Heights were part of Syria, describing Israeli occupation as “totally unacceptable.”

Al-Sharaa also used his second turn at the UN rostrum to denounce repeated Israeli strikes on his country since the fall of former dictator Bashar al-Assad.

“Israel is launching attacks against Syria. There have been 500 air strikes, more than 1,200 incursions, and 300 detentions. This is at odds with the orientation we’re seeing at global level,” he said.

“It is reminiscent of a era that we thought was long gone.”

World.title: Iraq urges Iran to defuse regional tensions through dialogue
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein emphasized to his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Araghchi, on Wednesday the importance of defusing regional tensions through dialogue.

Hussein’s remarks took place during his meeting with Araghchi in New York on the sidelines of their participation in the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Foreign Ministry.

The meeting addressed bilateral relations and regional developments, as well as the importance of continued coordination between the two countries to respond to current challenges and support diplomatic efforts aimed at enhancing regional stability.

Hussein stressed the significance of continued diplomatic efforts among the parties involved to defuse tension, prevent escalation, and maintain regional stability.

Araghchi outlined the discussions that began between Iran and the United States, sponsored by an intermediary, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly meetings in New York. These discussions attempt to de-escalate the situation and find approaches to reopen the Strait of Hormuz for navigation.

The two sides discussed the outcomes of the meeting involving the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states, Iraq, Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, Egypt, and Turkey—attended by US President Donald Trump—as well as how regional and international relationships might help efforts for de-escalation.

The two ministers emphasized the importance of supporting diplomatic efforts aimed at preventing escalation, defusing tensions, and fostering opportunities for dialog and peaceful solutions.

World.title: China’s Yu, 13, wins third gold with latest Asian Games record
World.content:
Tokyo – China’s 13-year-old swimming sensation Yu Zidi completed a hat-trick of Asian Games golds on Wednesday with a dominant victory in the 400m individual medley, two years out from the Los Angeles Olympics.

The school girl powered home in an Asian Games-record 4min 28.56sec to make it a clean sweep from her three individual events in Tokyo, following victories in the 200m butterfly and 200m individual medley, also in Games-record times.

She beat the previous 400m IM Games record set by China’s Ye Shiwen in 2014 by almost 4.5 seconds.

It was the fourth-fastest time in the world this year, with world record-holder Summer McIntosh owning the top three.

Yu is shaping up to be a major medal threat at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.

She has been the talk of swimming since becoming the youngest medallist in world championships history last year with bronze for China’s relay team aged just 12.

She also finished just outside the medals in fourth in three world individual events.

She has embellished her growing reputation this year, notably with a victory over multiple American Olympic champion Regan Smith in March.

She has dominated this week in Tokyo and gave another glimpse of her immense talent in the 400m IM.

Yu took the lead straight from the start and set off on a procession towards the finish line.

She finished 3.95sec clear of silver medallist Ke Wenxi of China, with Japan’s Mio Narita finishing third.

As well as international news headlines, her Asian Games exploits have caused a sensation back home.

Her back story, such as being spotted by chance by a swimming coach at a water park, and her struggle with interviews, have gone viral.

Asked if answering questions was the hardest part, she replied with a giggle this week: “Every time I just want to float off somewhere else.”

World.title: China’s Xi heads to US for talks with Trump: state media
World.content:
Beijing – China’s leader Xi Jinping departed Beijing on Wednesday, bound for Washington where he will meet with US President Donald Trump, state media said.

The highly anticipated talks come as the two countries confront rising fears about increasingly capable artificial intelligence systems, and as both sides look to ease tensions on trade.

Xi “left Beijing by special plane”, accompanied by his wife Peng Liyuan, his right-hand man Cai Qi, and foreign minister Wang Yi, among others, state broadcaster CCTV said.

Trump is due to personally meet Xi on his arrival at Joint Base Andrews, before their meetings on Thursday, according to the White House.

The US leader was greeted by China’s vice president when he landed in Beijing for his state visit in May.

Xi and Peng will attend a ceremony at the White House on Thursday morning, which will include a military flyover.

The two leaders are due to hold talks and Trump is set to host Xi for a state dinner at the White House in the evening.

The visit will wrap up on Friday morning where the two presidential couples will have tea at the White House then visit the National Archives to round out the trip.

The White House said that the visit marks “a significant milestone in the relationship between the two countries.”

But the meeting between the two leaders could touch on multiple points of tension, with Trump telling reporters that he will be “discussing almost everything” with Xi.

Trump’s Iran war casts a long shadow, as China seeks to avoid US sanctions against countries dealing with Tehran — despite reports that Beijing supplied Tehran with intelligence for a strike on US troops.

A trade war is of even greater concern and the world’s two largest economies are still seeking to mitigate the fallout from Trump’s global tariffs.

The threat of war over the island of Taiwan — which China claims as its territory — looms large as well.

– Leverage –

Analysts, however, have tempered expectations by cautioning there might not be many concrete deals announced.

Preliminary talks between US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and his Chinese counterpart He Lifeng discussed creating a communication channel for AI concerns, but released little in the way of detail.

Bessant said at the time that the two sides discussed setting up a way to communicate about AI issues called the “US-China AI dialogue.”

“The US has proposed that we have a notification mechanism between the two countries,” Bessent said.

The son of jailed Hong Kong pro-democracy media mogul Jimmy Lai made an appeal to Xi from Washington that his 78-year-old father be released.

Trump said in May, however, that he had discussed Lai’s fate with Xi and his release was unlikely.

But Beijing did release the founder of an underground church, Ezra Jin, after Trump raised his case with Xi.

China’s negotiating arsenal includes its dominance in the supply of rare earths, critical materials used for high-tech products that are vital to US manufacturers.

Beijing successfully pressured Washington to back down from its sky-high tariffs last year after imposing stringent controls on exports of rare earths.

World.title: Iraq to restructure financial policy
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi confirmed on Tuesday that the government is moving forward with restructuring the country’s financial policy.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during his meeting with the Director of the Middle East and Central Asia Department at the International Monetary Fund (IMF), Jihad Azour, on the sidelines of his participation in the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, which opened on Tuesday in New York.

The meeting addressed developments in the global economy and the repercussions of the crisis currently affecting the region, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The discussions also addressed the effects on markets, supply chains, and inflation rates, in addition to the impacts on energy consumption and oil prices.

Al-Zaidi highlighted that the government is focused on expanding automation systems and is gradually shifting toward a program-and-performance-based budget as part of the 2027 budget initiative.

Azour reaffirmed the IMF’s willingness to continue working with Iraq and support the path of economic and fiscal reforms, contributing to the country’s financial and economic stability.

The IMF projected in July that the Iraqi economy will be the most hit by oil and transportation disruptions in the Middle East and Central Asia in 2026.

The IMF also predicted a robust economic rebound in 2027, when energy market conditions improve and commerce resumes.

The anticipated fall in 2026 will mainly result from the disruption in oil production and distribution, especially by countries that depend heavily on energy exports, but the recovery in 2027 will be brought about by a reduction of these shocks and resumption of business activities.

World.title: After split verdict, SC refers law on EC appointment to larger bench; decision comes amid row over EC functioning
World.content:
NEW DELHI: On a day when

found itself under the scanner, a two-judge bench of

gave a split verdict on whether the issue of validity of the law on appointment of CEC/ECs be referred to a constitution bench, but later agreed to refer the case to a larger bench for the sake of early adjudication of the contentious issue.

Validity of several provisions of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 has been challenged on the ground that the law gives the executive "overwhelming" power to appoint its nominee as election commissioner, as the selection panel composed of the PM, a Cabinet minister and the leader of the opposition is designed to give govt a 2:1 majority.

The petitioners contended that EC's independence would be compromised in this process.

The 2023 law was framed to replace an SC verdict which had directed that selection be done by a committee of the PM, CJI and leader of the opposition until Parliament determined the composition by passing a law. "Speaking in one voice would have better served institutional cohesion. Unfortunately, the court is divided in its opinion," a bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and S C Sharma said.





The hearing in the case went on for five days and at the fag end of proceedings, the Centre had sought referral of the case to a constitution bench.

SC: Constitution bench should deal with case to prevent delay

Noting that appointment of CEC/ECs was being litigated for last 11 years in SC after a petition was filed in 2015, the bench decided that the case should not be referred to a three-judge bench, which is the normal procedure, but to a constitution bench to settle the issue once and for all.

It reasoned that a decision by a three-judge bench would be of little worth and only delay adjudication of the significant issue(s) that these writ petitions raise.

"Thus, we direct that the papers be placed before the CJI for considering the desirability of constituting a constitution bench of such number of judges to decide the question of vires of Sec 7 and the other provisions of Act," the bench said.

The bench expressed hope that the case would be given priority as the issues raised were of "foundational importance to the democratic fabric of the country and its citizenry".

"Petitioners seem to be justified in expressing their anxiety that references to five-judge benches remain unresolved for years. If statistics are any guide, none can say with any reasonable degree of certainty when long-pending references will get resolved. Undisputedly, this is an area of grave concern and the inordinate delay in resolution of the references is itself a source of institutional embarrassment which all stakeholders ought to strive to avoid.

Self-introspection, indeed, is required," it said.

"We, thus, take this opportunity of requesting the Chief Justice to also explore the necessity of constituting a permanent five-judge bench to decide pure constitutional issues. This is not something novel that we are saying. It has been opined time and again by responsible citizens and we simply endorse their opinion. Given that resolving constitutional issues is the primary task of judges of this court, that must remain its core priority.

World.title: EC faultlines have a long history, dating back to 1989
World.content:
Election Commission of India

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: It is not the first time that faultlines within the Election Commission are out in the open. The trend started from the time it became a multi-member body in 1989, reports Bharti Jain.Two election commissioners S S Dhanoa and V S Seigell were appointed in Oct 1989 and joined EC then led by chief election commissioner (CEC) R V S Peri Sastri. It is widely believed the new arrangement was perceived by Shastri as a dilution in power. By Jan 1990, their appointments were rescinded, and EC reverted to being a single-member body.In 1993, with T N Seshan as an all-powerful CEC, the commission was once again made a multi-member body with appointment of ECs M S Gill and G V G Krishnamurthy. What followed was a running feud between Seshan on the one hand and Gill and Krishnamurthy on the other. It was on Seshan's plea challenging govt's decision to make EC a multi-member body that the SC had, in 1995, ruled that the election commissioners and CEC were equal in status, power, and decision-making authority and that CEC was only "first among equals".The other internal feud in EC to recall would be one between then CEC N Gopalaswami and election commissioner Navin Chawla between 2006 and 2009. Months before he was to step down, Gopalaswami wrote to the President recommending the removal of Chawla for a pro-Congress bias.Differences cropped up between then CEC Sunil Arora and then EC Ashok Lavasa, both appointees of Modi govt, during the 2019 LS polls. Lavasa resigned on Aug 18, 2020, two years short of his tenure.

World.title: Cong-led oppn demands Gyanesh ouster, Supreme Court probe
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress Wednesday led the opposition in demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar be sacked and an SC-monitored probe be ordered into the "rot", amid reports that two ECs repeatedly opposed various steps taken about SIR.

The opposition announced it will move "impeachment motions" against Kumar whenever a "special session" of Parliament is called. It underlined that a removal notice against Kumar, submitted in April, is pending with the Rajya Sabha chairperson. Mamata Banerjee, CPM's John Brittas, CPI(ML)'s Dipankar Bhattacharya, DMK's M K Stalin, Sena (UBT)'s Uddhav Thackeray, NCP(SP)'s Supriya Sule, CPI's D Raja, AAP and SP demanded SIR be halted.

With vote chori,

, RSS & EC committed act of treason:

Sources said the INDIA bloc will jointly take forward the fight against CEC. LoP Rahul Gandhi said, "Vote chori is a crime against people and a direct attack on our Constitution. BJP, RSS and EC who organised it have committed act of treason. Justice will be served." Mamata said Kumar should be arrested, while TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee demanded a "look out circular" be issued against the CEC to prevent him from "fleeing".





Stalin said Kumar had no right to continue in office and must resign. He sought a fair probe "into everything that transpired within EC", adding those responsible should be held accountable. Terming the reports' findings "explosive", he said it cast "serious doubts" over the results of every assembly election held after the SIR exercise.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and MP Abhishek Singhvi said the opposition has been raising questions about the fairness of elections and EC's role for a long time, but their concerns went unheeded.

"Misuse of Form 6, misuse of software, tampering with voter lists, decisions without transparency - these are all now in front of the country. Then what did the CEC do about these objections? In the first three phases of SIR, 13.8 crore names were removed from draft electoral rolls of 31 states and UTs."

Party general secretary K C Venugopal said, "How the hell can one man, acting on his master's orders, strike off names at whim? How can he sideline fellow constitutional officers to take blatantly illegal steps that put our democracy in danger?"

Singhvi said the revelations are an example of a "double bulldozer sarkar". He said while an external bulldozer works against institutions, an internal bulldozer is CEC who bulldozed his own organisation and colleagues and "hijacked" EC. He said SC has clearly ruled that all election commissioners, including the CEC, function on equal footing, and the revelations about the watchdog's functioning show that election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, who dissented against the CEC were in a majority.

World.title: BJP defends EC, says oppn trying to discredit panel
World.content:
He said opposition parties had questioned the functioning of the three election commissioners both when they appeared to agree and now when correspondence between them has emerged.

NEW DELHI: Differences of opinion within EC are a sign of its democratic functioning, BJP said Wednesday as it mounted a strong counter-charge against the Opposition over its attack on the poll body and govt, saying its rivals have been trying to discredit institutions since 2014, including before the rollout of SIR, due to their dwindling popular support."If there is no discussion of any kind among three election commissioners and they simply agree to everything, then these very opposition parties will call it dictatorship and claim that they were all 'yes men' because they were appointed by govt," BJP's Sambit Patra said.Now, the media has reported their correspondences as a divergence of views on the appropriateness of some measures taken by the commission, and this is a sign of a healthy democracy, he added.Targeting the Opposition for its allegation that BJP's impressive run of recent poll victories was aided by SIR, he said, "The statistics from Bengal expose the Opposition's narrative of 'vote chori', as TMC won 13 of the 20 seats with the highest number of deleted voters, while BJP won only six." Opposition's outrage is an outcome of its receding influence since 2014, when PM Modi led NDA to a huge victory, he said.BJP also cited alleged links of several past ECs, including ex-CECs M S Gill and Navin Chawla, to Congress during its long stint in office.

World.title: US ambassador to India Sergio Gor makes rare appearance at event hosted by Chinese envoy

Sergio Gor

NEW DELHI: US ambassador to India Sergio Gor made a rare appearance at a Chinese event here on Wednesday, as White House rolled out a red carpet for President Xi Jinping for a potentially landmark visit.Gor joined Chinese ambassador Xu Feihong for a reception hosted by the latter at a 5-star hotel to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of People's Republic of China. India's commerce secretary, Rajesh Aggarwal, was the chief guest. Russian ambassador Denis Alipov was also present.Unlike on such occasions in recent years, the anniversary saw a heavy presence of top Western diplomats, including the envoys of Germany, Canada and Netherlands.Xu reiterated Beijing's position that India and China were partners, not rivals. "

World.title: Cannot direct Speaker but expect early ruling on TMC rebels: Supreme Court
World.content:
Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Wednesday remarked that it expected Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla to take an "expeditious" decision on a plea seeking the disqualification of 20 rebel TMC MPs who have joined Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI).A bench comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said it was aware that it could not issue a direction to the Lok Sabha Speaker, "but we just want to remind him about an expeditious resolution".Senior advocate Kalyan Banerjee, representing TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee, submitted that the rebel parliamentarians had not filed a response despite notices being issued and had sought further extension.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Speaker, told SC that Birla had issued notices on the disqualification petitions. "He knows the seriousness of the matter," Mehta said.The CJI remarked, "We will expect anything which is required to be decided expeditiously, the very nature... demands early adjudication."Mehta responded, "Can a constitutional functionary remind another constitutional functionary of his constitutional duty?" He said the court should not prescribe a time limit for the Speaker.Justice Bagchi said, "...We may not give imperative directions, but keeping in mind the decision in the Keisham Meghachandra Singh case... have resolution of this issue expeditiously."In the 2020 case, SC had ruled that the speaker must decide defection cases within a reasonable time, preferably three months.Justice Bagchi asked Mehta to submit a timeline for the Speaker's decision. Mehta, however, said he could not give SC a commitment. "This court's monitoring may not be justified. I would urge not to fix the Speaker's schedule," he said.The top court recorded the submission of the rebel MPs that they would file a reply within four weeks and adjourned the matter.

Representative image

NEW DELHI: Private fuel retailers have started rationing diesel sales at their outlets amid a surge in global crude prices, driven by supply constraints caused by the ongoing West Asia conflict. However, state-owned oil marketing companies Indian Oil, HPCL and BPCL confirmed there was no such restriction at their outlets.The impact is limited, as the three public sector oil companies operate around 90% of the more than one lakh fuel stations in the country.Several Jio-BP retail outlets TOI spoke to confirmed they had been directed to sell only 50 litres of diesel per customer. World.title: Delhi High Court issues contempt notice to two men for releasing dogs on local commissioner
World.content:
The DelhiHigh Court has issued a contempt notice to two men for obstructing the work of a court-appointed local commissioner by releasing dogs on her when she went to inspect a property in the Mehrauli area of the Capital.

Justice Amit Bansal asked the two men to file affidavits in four weeks explaining why action should not be initiated against them for violating and wilfully disobeying judicial orders, and ordered them to be physically present in court on November 19.

In July, the court had asked the local commissioner to verify whether any construction was being undertaken at the property in the Mehrauli area.

In her report, the local commissioner, a practising advocate, submitted that when she reached the property for an inspection in terms of the High Court’s order in the case concerning a property dispute, distasteful remarks were hurled at her in an aggressive tone.

The report stated that two dogs were released from a kennel on the property and were put back in the enclosure after the head constable accompanying her intervened.

“This is a serious matter where dogs have been released on a local commissioner appointed by this court, as well as the photographer accompanying her. Along with the aforesaid report, the local commissioner has placed on record photos and videos evidencing the obstruction... in execution of the commission,” said the court in the order passed on September 18.

“The conduct of the appellants, as highlighted by the local commissioner, is a serious issue which prima facie shows that the appellants have caused obstruction in the execution of the commission appointed by this court. In this view of the matter, I deem it appropriate to issue notice to the appellants as to why action should not be taken against them under the Contempt of Courts Act,” the court said.

World.title: Arunachal Pradesh State Cabinet approves panel for survey of Siang mega dam
World.content:
GUWAHATI

Amid protests, the Arunachal Pradesh State Cabinet on Wednesday (September 23, 2026) adopted a resolution approving the constitution of an Empowered High-Level Committee “to guide and coordinate” the pre-feasibility report survey and associated activities for the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project or SUMP.

Villagers along the Siang River belt are resisting the pre-feasibility report for the project, which will generate an estimated 11,000 megawatts (MW) or more of hydroelectricity. Two of the project’s three designated sites are in Siang district, and one is in Upper Siang district.

The State Cabinet, headed by Chief Minister Pema Khandu, noted that the Union government had declared SUMP to be a national project in 2008, underlining its strategic significance for the country. It also noted that the project could strengthen water and energy security, help mitigate floods in the Siang-Brahmaputra basin, generate employment, and support long-term socio-economic development of the Siang region.

“The resolution reflects the State government’s continuing commitment to ensuring that the survey is carried out in a transparent, peaceful, and people-centric manner,” a statement from the Chief Minister’s Office said.

The Cabinet underlined concerns raised by some sections of the people in Siang and Upper Siang districts “regarding misinformation and disinformation” being spread by certain vested interests. It resolved that conducting the pre-feasibility report peacefully depended on sustained, meaningful engagement with the residents of these two districts.

“The voices, welfare, and aspirations of the likely project-affected families and local communities have always been, and will always remain, central to the process,” the State Cabinet said.

Meanwhile, local authorities organised a series of interactive school exhibitions on the SUMP, involving 640 students across four schools in Siang district. “The exhibitions formed part of a targeted educational outreach initiative to foster awareness about river management, sustainable hydropower, and the SUMP among students in Rumgong, Kaying and Pessing villages that may be affected by the project,” an official statement said.

The Centre and State governments have defended the SUMP, insisting it was needed to counter the 60,000 MW project China is constructing on the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet.

The Yarlung Tsangpo flows into Arunachal Pradesh as the Siang, which meets two other rivers — Dibang and Lohit — to form the Brahmaputra in Assam.

World.title: J&K observes holiday on Dogra king Hari Singh’s birthday; BJP holds special functions
World.content:
The BJP on Wednesday celebrated the birth anniversary of Dogra Maharaja Hari Singh and praised his move to accede to India in 1947. Meanwhile, Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah highlighted the role of party founder Sheikh Muhammad Abdullah, who was dropped from the official holiday list of J&K by the Lieutenant Governor’s (LG) administration.

The BJP held a series of functions in Srinagar and Jammu on the occasion. Speaking on the birth anniversary of the Dogra Maharaja, BJP leader and J&K Waqf Board chairperson Darakshan Andrabi said, “Maharaja Hari Singh took the wise decision in 1947 by acceding to India. How much have we benefited from the decision. Today we are with India, our country,” said Ms. Andrabi.

Ms. Andrabi described Mr. Singh’s rule as inclusive. “In his court, there were Hindus, Muslims, Sikhs, Christians. Everyone had to get equal rights,” said Ms. Andrabi.

J&K Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha also paid homage to the Maharaja in a message on X. “Maharaja Hari Singh was an enlightened statesman and progressive thinker who introduced several significant reforms focused on the welfare and empowerment of the people. His principles of public service, equality and inclusive development continue to hold significance and inspire people,” said Mr. Sinha.

There was an official holiday in J&K on the birth anniversary of the Maharaja on September 23. It was included in the holiday list by the Lieutenant Governor’s administration in 2022. However, the birth and death anniversaries of National Conference (NC) founder Sheikh Abdullah as holidays were dropped from the list, which has sparked strong reaction from the NC.

NC legislator Tanvir Sadiq questioned the move to drop Mr. Abdullah’s anniversaries as holidays. “It doesn’t take a rocket scientist to see the irony. A leader associated with land reforms that empowered the tiller and transferred land ownership to the poor has his holiday removed, while a holiday commemorating the ruler under whose reign Kashmiris endured repression is celebrated. No hatred. No prejudice. Just history. Facts are facts,” said Mr. Sadiq.

J&K CM Abdullah said Sheikh Abdullah’s role in J&K’s history was well known. “The sacrifices made by the NC could not be forgotten. No one can forget the role of Sher-e-Kashmir here. The BJP was attempting to present history differently whenever it disagreed with a particular narrative,” said Mr. Abdullah.

He said to those people who didn’t take part in the fight for freedom, what lesson will they teach us? “RSS and the ancestral party of BJP, everyone knows their role in the fight for freedom. Everyone knows who apologised and what they did,” he added.

World.title: Bihar BJP MLA criticises own government for distributing ₹10,000 crore to JEEVIKA didis
World.content:
BiharBharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLA from Lauriya assembly constituency, Vinay Bihari, is not happy with his own government’s decision and criticised it for distributing ₹10000 crore to JEEViKA didis before the 2025 assembly election.

The former Minister also raised questions over the issues of age limits in politics, the salaries and pensions received by politicians, and the eligibility to contest elections.

His video, dated September 21, 2026, has gone viral on social media in which he is directly raising questions about the functioning of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government led by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary.

Speaking to the district reporters in Buxar, Mr. Bihari said, “If we are already doing developmental work and development is visible, then what was the need to distribute money during election time? Due to that, today’s developmental work is being hampered.”

He further argued that the development will take place if there is a burden of debt, and challenges will arise in mobilising resources for schemes in the future also.

Mr. Bihari also expressed apprehension that he may face disciplinary action for speaking against the government.

“For me, the Bharatiya Janata Party is like a temple; however, if something goes wrong even in a temple, my conscience tells me to speak out about it. I do not know whether I should speak or not, but speaking less will cost votes, speaking more will cost a ticket, and speaking excessively will cost your head. I do not know what the consequences of this statement would be, and I may be punished,”Mr. Bihari said.

Months before the Assembly election, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had launched the scheme through videoconferencing from Delhi and directly transferred ₹7,500 crore into the bank accounts of 75 lakh women across Bihar.

So far, the Nitish Kumar-led Bihar government has transferred money to over 1.81 crore women under Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana with an aim to empower women through financial assistance to start their own businesses. The opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) and Congress in Bihar have repeatedly accused the state government of winning the election by giving bribes before the election. More recently, the opposition has claimed that the state treasury is bankrupt due to freebies announced during the election.

Earlier Mr. Bihari had criticised the government over prohibition in the state. He had said that liquor was being sold everywhere in Bihar and police were very much aware about it. He had even demanded review of the prohibition law.

The BJP MLA also questioned how a person in prison could contest elections, whereas an ordinary citizen in jail is barred from voting. He asked about salaries and pensions received by politicians, given that politics is supposed to be a form of public service. Mr. Bihari asked why there should be provisions for salary and pension in return for such service.

Asked about party MLA speaking the language of opposition, Bihar BJP spokesperson Kuntal Krishna told The Hindu, “There is 100% democracy in our party but there are places, there are times, there are issues on which everyone is free to tell. You have to be conscious about the place and issue where you are speaking. Democracy does not mean that you will speak whatever you want. There is no scarcity of funds in the state, and he may not be aware of it. JEEViKA didis deserved that; they have done excellent work in Bihar and have created the domestic market of nearly ₹60000 crore.”

RJD spokesperson Ejaz Ahmed supported the BJP MLA’s stand, saying that he spoke from his conscience and alleged that the NDA has formed the government by giving bribes to women before the election.

World.title: CM Fadnavis and DCM Shinde visit drought-prone regions in Maharashtra
World.content:
A Latur farmer broke down in the presence of Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis during his visit to Latur district in the Marathwada region to assess the drought-like situation. Elsewhere, Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde visited Akola district on Wednesday.

The tour of CM and DCM comes after Mr. Fadnavis on Tuesday (September 22), announced the formation of a subcommittee to handle the drought issue under the chairmanship of Revenue Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule, while issuing a drought GR by Saturday (September 26) announcing the financial assistance for the farmers, who faced crop loss due to long dry spell.

Nilanga, a taluka-based farmer, sobbingly said, “Pani nahi, nuksan jhala ahe (No water, suffering heavy losses.”

Giving assurance to the farmer, Mr. Fadnavis said, “In the next two days, the drought government resolution will be issued, providing relief to farmers. The focus will be to provide assistance to farmers for rabi crops and make availability of drinking water, fodder for cattle, and food grains.”

Mr. Fadnavis on Wednesday (September 23) visited Nilanga taluka in Latur and Dharashiv districts, which received around 50% rainfall. “Latur is the worst hit by drought this year and received less rainfall compared to last year, when the rainfall was at least 65% to 70%. This has caused crop loss,” Mr. Fadnavis added.

Eknath Shinde visits Akola

Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde visited Akola district and said, “There is no alternative but to announce a drought after witnessing the situation. Last year also farmers suffered due to heavy downpour, and I stood with them; this year also I will stand behind them. Will do whatever is required to do as farmers also have the right to the State government treasury.

According to State government data, the State is at present witnessing a 17% rainfall deficit, as it has recorded 787.2 mm of rainfall against a normal rainfall of 953.2 mm. Several regions in the Marathwada region, including Latur, have received less than 50% rainfall. The deficient rainfall in the State is being attributed to El Niño.

The opposition leader NCP-SP Rohit Pawar, who has been leading a protest to declare a drought in the State, responded to the plight of the farmer, saying, “It is heart-wrenching to see a farmer breaking down before the Chief Minister”. Highlighting the demand of ₹50,000 per hectare to farmers and Rs 25,000 per family to agricultural labourers, he added, “I have been witnessing all this from last eight to ten days in Vidarbha and Marathwada.”

While NCP-SP MP Supriya Sule credited NCP (SP) Supremo and her father Sharad Pawar for writing to Mr. Fadnavis and said, “The action have been taken only after Sharad Pawar raised the issue with the government through his letter.

World.title: Xi arrives in Washington, kicking off his state visit with rare planeside welcome from Trump
World.content:
Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in Washington on Wednesday (September 23, 2026), where he was to be met with a rare planeside greeting from U.S. President Donald Trump, who was there to welcome his counterpart on the tarmac instead of waiting for him to drive up to the White House.

Mr. Trump's decision to greet Mr. Xi at Joint Base Andrews just outside Washington rather than receiving him at the executive residence shows how far the U.S. President is going to honour China's leader as he made his first state visit to the U.S. capital in more than a decade.

The U.S. President and first lady Melania Trump were at the base to participate in an arrival ceremony for Mr. Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan. The salutation kicks off a three-day visit that's expected to be saturated with pomp, even by White House standards. The state visit, complete with a formal state dinner at the White House on Thursday, is supposed to reciprocate the ceremonial grandeur that marked Mr. Trump's May visit to China.

But it is also a showy patina at a time when tensions between the two geopolitical rivals are high over trade, artificial intelligence, Trump's war with Iran and China's designs on Taiwan.

The visit comes after Mr. Trump's trip to China in May
